301	### 2026-05-29 — perf-log USB throughput: multi-IRP, drain refactor, Fletcher-16, single MAX_BYTES
302	
303	Day-long push to unblock perf-log throughput beyond the ~1.88 MB/s ceiling that the journal's [2026-05-22 USB CDC bandwidth headroom](#2026-05-22--usb-cdc-bandwidth-headroom--state-queue-starvation-diagnosis) entry diagnosed. Outcome on hardware (185×32 sensing + 290×32 strike strips, 60 fps, 20 s capture): **2.77 MB/s sustained, zero drops anywhere, every record type flowing at 100% of its design rate, ts_counter inversions bounded to 5 ms (queue-interleave noise only), drain CPU recovered from ~26% (soft CRC) to ~2% (Fletcher), UI responsive again**. Several discrete landings, documented in causal order along with the diagnostic that drove each.
304	
305	| Metric (185×32 + 290×32 strips, 20 s) | Before this session | After |
306	|---|---|---|
307	| Sustained wire | 1.88 MB/s ceiling, ~700 state drops/s | **2.77 MB/s, no ceiling reached, 0 state drops** |
308	| Sink drops | 0 at 1.88, climbing above | **0**, headroom remaining |
309	| Strip drops | growing at higher dims | **0** |
310	| Frame-side stamps | 71% delivery (CV_END worst at 8%) | **100%** (60.0/s exactly) |
311	| FBL_SEND / CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE | 71% | **100%** (240/s exactly) |
312	| HWM/RUNTIME records | absent (lost at state queue) | **5/s each, flowing** |
313	| ts_counter inversion p99 | 7,345 ms (queue lag) | **5.2 ms** (drain-cycle interleave only) |
314	| Drain CPU on CRC | ~26% (soft, bit-by-bit) | **~2%** (Fletcher) |
315	
316	**Multi-IRP pipelining via UDPHS driver patch.** The journal's "lever 1" hypothesis (pipeline CDC writes for 2-3× win) had a hidden gotcha. The CDC layer accepts multiple in-flight IRPs (`queueSizeWrite` and `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED` are both knobs), but the underlying UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch. Subsequent IRPs are linked into the endpoint's queue but *never armed for transmission* — `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after a callback fires but doesn't re-program the DMA hardware. Net effect: even with all three layers configured for N=3 in-flight, only one IRP ever transmitted; the other two sat as `STATUS_PENDING` in the linked list forever.
317	
318	Walked the IRPSubmit and Tasks_ISR_DMA paths line by line in [drv_usb_udphs_device.c](../default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c) before convincing myself this was a real driver-side limitation. Fix: extracted the existing inline DMA-arm code (~80 lines mirroring lines 1880-2008 of the IRPSubmit body) into a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` and added a call after the queue advance in two places — `Tasks_ISR_DMA` (DMA-completion ISR) and the ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR`. Patch markers (`/* PATCH: */`) make the change findable after MCC regen. Logged as **patch #9** in the re-apply list. False starts before getting here:
319	
320	- N=3 ring + counting semaphore + sink reject path (correct in principle, blocked by `queueSizeWrite=1` cap in MCC's emitted CDC init).
321	- Bumped combined queue depth to 5 + per-instance `queueSizeWrite` to 3 (correct, but blocked by missing DMA arm in driver).
322	- Patched the driver (real fix).
323	
324	The MCC-side prerequisites for the patch to do anything useful:
325	- `usb_device_cdc_0.yml` adds `CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_FUNCTION_WRITE_Q_SIZE = 3` (per-instance write queue).
326	- `usb_device_cdc.yml` adds `CONFIG_USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 5` (RX prime + write queue + serialState — exact fit, no slack).
327	- `usb_device_init_data.c` shows `.queueSizeWrite = 3` after regen.
328	- `configuration.h` shows `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 5U`.
329	All three are now in MCC yml — regen preserves them, no re-apply patch needed for the config side. Just the driver change is patch #9.

12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)
70	 * acts on. Only one active at a time, irrespective of how many are
71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
74	detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);

### 1. **Phototransistor Physical Placement** (Upstream of Strike)

**Location**: Fretboard PCB samples at the **sensing line** — above the strike-line region where notes are played.

The cv_marvin_v1 detector samples at **two screen rows**, both above the strike:

**A. Sensing strip** (y=311 in 720×480 frame space):

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:395-404*

```
- "Sensing strip centers on the sensor row (y=311); strike strip is below the sensors at the strum trigger zone"
- **Strike strip is sampled for visualization only** — not used in detection logic (cv_marvin_v1 only reads y=311)

---

### 3. **Frame_Epoch Alignment: Detector vs. ADC Samples**

Both record `frame_epoch` (video frame count), but **at different rates**, creating a many-to-one mapping:

| Component | Rate | Record Type | Frame Epoch | Timestamp |
|-----------|------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| CV Detector | 60 Hz (~16.7 ms) | PERF_REC_DETECTOR | `frame.frame_count` | `xTaskGetTickCount() * US_PER_TICK` |
| Fretboard ADC | 240 Hz (~4.17 ms) | PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW | `Video_GetFrameInfo().frame_count` (same as CV) | `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()` (ISR) |

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:156-157*  
*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:348-350*

**Behavior**: Approximately **4 consecutive FRETBOARD_RAW records** carry the **same frame_epoch** as one DETECTOR record (240 ÷ 60 = 4).

### 4. **SensiML CSV Export: Label Propagation Method**

The exporter performs a **step-function forward-fill** of detector labels across fretboard samples:

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py:100-124*

```python
if isinstance(rec, Detector):
    last_detector = rec
    n_detector_records += 1
    continue

if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
    # ... timestamp calc ...
    pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
    row = [
        f"{t_s:.6f}",
        rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
        (pressed >> 0) & 1,  # Extract bit for each fret
        (pressed >> 1) & 1,
        ...
    ]
    writer.writerow(row)
```

**CSV Schema** (11 columns):
- `timestamp` — seconds since SESSION record
- `ph_green` ... `ph_orange` — 5× ADC values (0–4095, lower = note)
- `label_green` ... `label_orange` — 5× binary fret-pressed flags (from DETECTOR.pressed_mask)

**Example (test case)** from `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_export_sensiml_csv.py:69-71`:
- Epoch 1: `pressed=0b00000` → all labels = 0 → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 0,0,0,0,0]`
- Epoch 2: `pressed=0b00001` (green) → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 1,0,0,0,0]`
- Epoch 3: `pressed=0b00101` (green + yellow) → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 1,0,1,0,0]`

---

### 5. **Strum Timing: Commands vs. Firings (Not Currently Recorded)**

The current perf-log captures **when marvin emits button-press commands**, not **when fretboard physically asserts strum GPIO**:

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:417-432*

```c
void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
{
    // ... queue mask ...
    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
}
```

**PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record** (*perf_log_records.h:330-343*):
- `intended_mask` — the command being sent
- `asserted_mask` — last successfully transmitted byte (tracked as `s_last_sent_byte`)
- `strum_dir` — direction (0=none, 1=down, 2=up)
- `producer_id` — TIMING (pipeline) or others
- `last_ack_result` — USB CDC result
- `last_ack_ts_counter` — when the CDC write completed

**Critical gap**: No record of **when the fretboard GPIO actually fires** or **when the strum solenoid energizes**. The CSV exporter ignores PERF_REC_ACTUATOR entirely — **strum timing is not a training label or input feature**.

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py:1-19*: Comment states "label = cv_marvin_v1 pressed_mask" — no mention of strum data.

---

### 6. **The Misalignment Problem: Spatial Offset**

Notes scroll down the screen from top to bottom. The detector at y=311 and the physical fretboard phototransistors see the same note at **different times**:

1. Note appears high on screen → fretboard ADC sees it (note approaching y=311)
2. ~50–100 ms later → CV detector at y=311 sees it
3. ~100–150 ms later → Strike line (y~450) reached; strum should fire

**Current CSV export aligns by frame_epoch only**, which compresses 4.17 ms of ADC data into a single detector label. **No sub-frame temporal correction** is applied.

---

### 7. **What Fields Exist Today vs. Missing**

| Aspect | Recorded | Missing |
|--------|----------|---------|
| CV detector (y=311) output per frame | ✓ PERF_REC_DETECTOR (60 Hz) | Sub-frame timing within detector frame |
| Fretboard ADC raw samples | ✓ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (240 Hz) | ADC sample jitter / actual sample timestamps |
| Frame alignment token | ✓ `frame_epoch` (common) | Spatial offset between sensor regions |
| Strum command intent | ✓ PERF_REC_ACTUATOR | Strum GPIO firing time (fretboard-side) |
| Strum result (ACK) | ✓ USB CDC write-complete | Physical strum solenoid energization |
| Strike-line occupancy | ~ PERF_STRIP_STRIKE (visualization only) | Unused in detection; no binary label |
| Label propagation | ✓ Forward-fill (SensiML CSV) | Temporal interpolation for note descent |

---

### Bottom Line

**The misalignment is a spatial causality issue**: the fretboard phototransistors (above strike, at unknown y) detect notes before the cv_detector (y=311) and way before the strike line. The SensiML CSV exporter currently:
- Assigns a **single binary label per 4-sample ADC window** (step function forward-fill)
- Does **not model the note-descent trajectory** or the ~50–150 ms offset between detection regions
- Does **not include strum timing** as a label or feature

For improved ML training, you'd need either:
1. **Temporal shift correction**: Measure or estimate the pixel-scroll rate and offset ADC labels backward in time
2. **Spatial ROI labels**: Add strikes at y=212 (strum line) as a secondary binary label
3. **Strum event capture**: Log fretboard GPIO assertions or solenoid current from the fretboard MCU

85	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration

87	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
88	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
89	{
90	    int cx = (int)px;
91	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
92	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
93	    int cy = (int)py;
94	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
95	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
96	
97	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
98	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
99	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
100	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
101	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
102	
103	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
104	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
105	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
106	    {
107	        const uint8_t *row = frame
108	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
109	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
110	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
111	        {
112	            sum_b += row[0];
113	            sum_g += row[1];
114	            sum_r += row[2];
115	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
116	        }
117	    }
118	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
119	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
120	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
121	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
122	}

124	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
125	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
126	{
127	    float m = bgr[0];
128	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
129	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
130	    return m;
131	}

133	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
134	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
135	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
136	{
137	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
138	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
139	    float cmin = bgr[0];
140	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
141	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
142	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
143	
144	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
145	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
146	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
147	    return (target - reject) * sat;
148	}

1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	The firmware deliberately contains **no game logic** — it only scans
13	ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks.
14	
15	## Hardware
16	
17	### Target
18	
19	| Spec | Value |
20	|------|-------|
21	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
22	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
23	| Clock | 24 MHz |
24	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
25	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
26	
27	### Pin Map
28	
29	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
30	
31	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
32	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
33	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
34	presence.
35	
36	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
37	|---------|-----------|-----|
38	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
39	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
40	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
41	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
42	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
43	
44	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
45	
46	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
47	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
48	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
49	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
50	
51	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
52	|----------|-----|---------|
53	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
54	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
55	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
56	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
57	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
58	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
59	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
60	
61	#### UART (SERCOM1)
62	
63	| Function | Pin |
64	|----------|-----|
65	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
66	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
67	
68	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
69	
70	## Software Architecture
71	
72	### Processing Loop
73	
74	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
75	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
76	timer ISR:
77	
78	```
79	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
80	    |
81	    v
82	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
83	    |
84	    v
85	data_stream_send()       12-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
86	    |
87	    v
88	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
89	```
90	
91	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
92	
93	### Module Descriptions
94	
95	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
96	
97	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
98	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
99	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
100	
101	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
102	the firmware:
103	
104	```
105	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
106	```
107	
108	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
109	
110	Emits one 12-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
111	
112	| Offset | Size | Field |
113	|-------:|-----:|-------|
114	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
115	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
116	| 3 | 2 | red |
117	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
118	| 7 | 2 | blue |
119	| 9 | 2 | orange |
120	| 11 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
121	
122	The frame is dropped silently if the TX free-buffer count is below the
123	frame size. At 240 Hz this is 2 880 B/s — well within the 50 000 B/s
124	budget at 500 000 baud.
125	
126	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
127	
128	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
129	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
130	
131	| Bit | Output |
132	|----:|--------|
133	| 0 | Green fret |
134	| 1 | Red fret |
135	| 2 | Yellow fret |
136	| 3 | Blue fret |
137	| 4 | Orange fret |
138	| 5 | Strum down |
139	| 6 | Strum up |
140	
141	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
142	
143	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
144	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
145	the same tick are coalesced away.
146	
147	## Tools
148	
149	### Host-side data-stream monitor
150	
151	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
152	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
153	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
154	
155	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
156	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
157	needed:
158	
159	```
160	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
161	# or, equivalently:
162	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
163	```
164	
165	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
166	
167	## Build System
168	
169	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
170	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
171	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
172	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
173	
174	## File Map
175	
176	| File | Purpose |
177	|------|---------|
178	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
179	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
180	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
181	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
182	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
183	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
184	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
185	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
186
```

85	static inline bool note_q_empty(void) { return s_note_count == 0u; }
86	static inline bool note_q_full(void)  { return s_note_count >= TP_FIFO_CAP; }
87	static inline bool strum_q_empty(void){ return s_strum_count == 0u; }
88	static inline bool strum_q_full(void) { return s_strum_count >= TP_FIFO_CAP; }
89	
90	static void note_q_push(pending_note_t n)
91	{
92	    s_note_q[s_note_tail] = n;
93	    s_note_tail = (uint8_t)((s_note_tail + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
94	    s_note_count++;
95	}
96	
97	static void note_q_pop(void)
98	{
99	    s_note_head = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
100	    s_note_count--;
101	}
102	
103	static void strum_q_push(pending_strum_t s)
104	{
105	    s_strum_q[s_strum_tail] = s;
106	    s_strum_tail = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
107	    s_strum_count++;
108	}
109	
110	static void strum_q_pop(void)
111	{
112	    s_strum_head = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
113	    s_strum_count--;
114	}
115	
116	/* Iterator helpers for the "is this fret needed by an outstanding entry?"
117	 * release-suppression check below. */
118	static bool note_q_any_needs(uint8_t bit)
119	{
120	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
121	    {
122	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
123	        if (s_note_q[idx].fret_mask & bit) { return true; }
124	    }
125	    return false;
126	}
127	
128	static bool strum_q_any_needs(uint8_t bit)
129	{
130	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_strum_count; i++)
131	    {
132	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
133	        if (s_strum_q[idx].fret_mask & bit) { return true; }
134	    }
135	    return false;
136	}
137	
138	static void publish_mask(uint8_t mask)
139	{
140	    s_output_mask = mask;
141	    if (s_pipeline_enabled)
142	    {
143	        FretboardLink_Send(mask, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING);
144	    }
145	}
146	
147	/* Edge derivation:
148	 *   - presses_mask: rising edge (press_count change preferred; pressed-edge
149	 *     fallback if the detector doesn't expose press_count for that fret)
150	 *   - releases_mask: falling edge of pressed
151	 * confidence is unused by the pipeline but is the natural future home for
152	 * a quality gate; left untouched here. */
153	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
154	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
155	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
156	{
157	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
158	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
159	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
160	
161	    bool first = !s_press_count_seen;
162	
163	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
164	    {
165	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
166	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
167	
168	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
169	        uint16_t pc = state->fret[i].confidence;  /* placeholder slot */
170	        (void)pc;
171	
172	        /* press_count is private to the detector; for now we infer rising
173	         * edge from pressed transitions only. If a detector later exposes
174	         * a press_count via a side channel, plug it in here. */
175	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
176	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
177	
178	        s_prev_press_count[i] = state->fret[i].confidence;
179	    }
180	
181	    if (first) { s_press_count_seen = true; }
182	
183	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
184	    *presses_mask  = pm;
185	    *releases_mask = rm;
186	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
187	}
188	
189	static void chord_commit(void)
190	{
191	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
192	    {
193	        s_chord_open = false;
194	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
195	        return;
196	    }

199	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;

4	#include <stdint.h>

6	
7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via
11	 * FretboardLink_Send. One of several possible producers — game menu
12	 * control (spec §4.8) and manual test inputs share the same submit API.
13	 *
14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33	
34	/* Output gate. Default: true. When false, the pipeline still advances
35	 * internal state but suppresses the FretboardLink_Send call so a peer
36	 * producer (manual_control today, future game-state controller §4.8) can
37	 * own the wire. Internal state stays current so the next advance() after
38	 * re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame. */
39	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled);
40	
41	#endif

178	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }

82	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
83	
84	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
85	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
86	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
87	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
88	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
89	{
90	    int cx = (int)px;
91	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
92	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
93	    int cy = (int)py;
94	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
95	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
96	
97	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
98	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
99	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
100	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
101	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
102	
103	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
104	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
105	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
106	    {
107	        const uint8_t *row = frame
108	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
109	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
110	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
111	        {
112	            sum_b += row[0];
113	            sum_g += row[1];
114	            sum_r += row[2];
115	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
116	        }
117	    }
118	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
119	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
120	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
121	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
122	}
123	
124	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
125	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
126	{
127	    float m = bgr[0];
128	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
129	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
130	    return m;
131	}
132	
133	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
134	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
135	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
136	{
137	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
138	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
139	    float cmin = bgr[0];
140	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
141	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
142	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
143	
144	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
145	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
146	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
147	    return (target - reject) * sat;
148	}

150	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
151	
152	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
153	{
154	    detector_state_t state;
155	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
156	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
157	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
158	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
159	
160	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
161	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
162	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
163	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
164	
165	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
166	    {
167	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
168	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
170	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
171	
172	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
173	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
174	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
175	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
176	
177	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
178	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
179	
180	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
181	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
182	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
183	
184	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
185	
186	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
187	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
188	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
189	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
190	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
191	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
192	
193	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
194	        float h = hd;
195	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
196	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
197	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
198	    }
199	
200	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
201	
202	    /* Mirror the same per-frame decision into the perf-log so offline tools
203	     * (marvin-perf, export-ml) can join detector ground truth with sensor
204	     * input. raw_value/confidence already scale 0..65535 to match the
205	     * perf-log struct. masks are LSB-first per fret_t. Default-disabled at
206	     * boot like the other high-rate types; host enables via SET_TYPE_MASK. */
207	    uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
208	    uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
209	    uint8_t  pressed_mask = 0u;
210	    uint8_t  edge_active_mask = 0u;
211	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
212	    {
213	        hold_dist[i] = state.fret[i].raw_value;
214	        edge_dist[i] = state.fret[i].confidence;
215	        if (s_pressed[i])     { pressed_mask     |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
216	        if (s_edge_active[i]) { edge_active_mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
217	    }
218	    PerfLog_EmitDetector(state.frame_epoch, hold_dist, edge_dist,
219	                         pressed_mask, edge_active_mask);
220	}

241	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
242	                                 int x, int y,
243	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
244	{
245	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
246	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
247	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
248	}

250	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
251	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
252	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
253	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
254	{
255	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
256	    while (x >= y)
257	    {
258	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
259	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
260	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
261	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
262	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
263	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
264	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
265	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
266	        y++;
267	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
268	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
269	    }
270	}
271	
272	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
273	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
274	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
275	{
276	    int rr = radius * radius;
277	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
278	    {
279	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
280	        {
281	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
282	            {
283	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
284	            }
285	        }
286	    }
287	}

289	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
290	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
291	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
292	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
293	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
294	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
295	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
296	
297	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
298	{
299	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;

302	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];

309	
310	        if (s_pressed[i])
311	        {
312	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
313	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
314	        }
315	        if (s_edge_active[i])
316	        {
317	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
318	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);

320	    }

352	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
353	
354	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
355	{
356	    (void)param;
357	
358	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
359	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
360	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
361	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
362	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
363	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
364	    configASSERT(subscribed);
365	
366	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
367	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
368	
369	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
370	
371	    publish_detector_config();
372	
373	    for (;;)
374	    {
375	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
376	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
377	
378	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
379	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
380	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
381	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
382	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
383	
384	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
385	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
386	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
387	
388	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
389	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
390	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
391	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
392	         * directly from the setter path. */
393	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
394	
395	        /* Sensing strip centers on the sensor row (y=311); strike strip is
396	         * below the sensors at the strum trigger zone. Both pre-overlay so
397	         * the host viewer sees the same pixels the detector consumed. */
398	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
399	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
400	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
401	                                   265u, 300, 185u, 32u);

1	"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.
2	
3	One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
4	ADC values plus five binary labels (one per fret), where the label comes
5	from the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask broadcast forward by
6	frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame).
7	
8	CSV schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset:
9	    timestamp,ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
10	    label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
11	
12	`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the SESSION record's ts_counter.
13	
14	Edge cases:
15	- FretboardRaw records before any Detector record are emitted with all
16	  labels = 0 by default; pass strict=True to drop them instead.
17	- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
18	  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import csv
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from pathlib import Path
26	
27	from ..capture import open_capture
28	from ..decode import decode_record
29	from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
30	from ..records import Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
31	from ..transport import FileSource
32	
33	
34	_HEADER = (
35	    "timestamp",
36	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
37	    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
38	)
39	
40	
41	class ExportError(Exception):
42	    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class ExportStats:
47	    n_rows: int
48	    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
49	    n_detector_records: int
50	    n_fretboard_records: int
51	    t_start_s: float
52	    t_end_s: float
53	    timer_freq_hz: int
54	
55	    @property
56	    def duration_s(self) -> float:
57	        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s
58	
59	
60	def export_sensiml_csv(
61	    capture_path: str | Path,
62	    out_path: str | Path,
63	    *,
64	    strict: bool = False,
65	) -> ExportStats:
66	    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.
67	
68	    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
69	    Detector record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
70	    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts
71	    before cv_marvin_v1 has produced its first frame.
72	    """
73	    capture = open_capture(capture_path)
74	
75	    session: Session | None = None
76	    last_detector: Detector | None = None
77	    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
78	    n_detector_records = 0
79	    n_fretboard_records = 0
80	    n_rows = 0
81	    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
82	    t_end_s = 0.0
83	
84	    out_path = Path(out_path)
85	    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
86	        writer = csv.writer(fh)
87	        writer.writerow(_HEADER)
88	        stats = FrameStats()
89	
90	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
91	            try:
92	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
93	            except Exception:
94	                continue
95	
96	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
97	                session = rec
98	                continue
99	
100	            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
101	                last_detector = rec
102	                n_detector_records += 1
103	                continue
104	
105	            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
106	                n_fretboard_records += 1
107	                if session is None:
108	                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
109	                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
110	                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
111	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
112	                    continue
113	                if last_detector is None and strict:
114	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
115	                    continue
116	
117	                if t_baseline is None:
118	                    t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
119	                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(
120	                    session.timer_freq_hz
121	                )
122	                t_end_s = t_s
123	
124	                pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
125	                row = [
126	                    f"{t_s:.6f}",
127	                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
128	                    (pressed >> 0) & 1,
129	                    (pressed >> 1) & 1,
130	                    (pressed >> 2) & 1,
131	                    (pressed >> 3) & 1,
132	                    (pressed >> 4) & 1,
133	                ]
134	                writer.writerow(row)
135	                n_rows += 1
136	
137	    if session is None:
138	        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
139	        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
140	        try:
141	            out_path.unlink()
142	        except FileNotFoundError:
143	            pass
144	        raise ExportError(
145	            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
146	            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
147	        )
148	
149	    return ExportStats(
150	        n_rows=n_rows,
151	        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
152	        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
153	        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
154	        t_start_s=0.0 if n_rows > 0 else 0.0,
155	        t_end_s=t_end_s,
156	        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
157	    )
158
```

171	    )

175	        dropped_strip=dropped_strip,
176	        dropped_sink=dropped_sink,
177	    )

179

181	    _check(payload, TaskHighwater.SIZE, "TaskHighwater")
182	    task_id, _reserved, words = TaskHighwater._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
183	    return TaskHighwater(hdr=hdr, task_id=task_id, words=words)
184	
185	
186	def _decode_task_runtime(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskRuntime:
187	    _check(payload, TaskRuntime.SIZE, "TaskRuntime")
188	    task_id, state, priority, _reserved, run_time_counter, _reserved2 = (
189	        TaskRuntime._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
190	    )
191	    return TaskRuntime(
192	        hdr=hdr,
193	        task_id=task_id,
194	        state=state,
195	        priority=priority,
196	        run_time_counter=run_time_counter,
197	    )
198	
199	
200	def _decode_strip(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Strip:
201	    if len(payload) < STRIP_HDR_BYTES:
202	        raise DecodeError(
203	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} < header {STRIP_HDR_BYTES}"
204	        )
205	    x, y, w, h, kind, _reserved = _STRIP_BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
206	    expected_pixels = w * h * STRIP_BPP
207	    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
208	        raise DecodeError(
209	            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
210	        )
211	    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
212	    if len(payload) != expected_total:
213	        raise DecodeError(
214	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
215	            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
216	        )
217	    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
218	    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, bgr=bgr)
219	
220	
221	_DISPATCH = {
222	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
223	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
224	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
225	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
226	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
227	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
228	    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
229	    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
230	    RecordType.DETECTOR_CONFIG: _decode_detector_config,
231	    RecordType.ACTUATOR: _decode_actuator,
232	    RecordType.FRETBOARD_RAW: _decode_fretboard_raw,
233	}
234	
235	
236	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
237	    """Decode an FCS-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
238	
239	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified FCS and length sanity.
240	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
241	    firmware does not crash an older host.
242	    """
243	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
244	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
245	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
246	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
247	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
248	
249	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
250	    if decoder is None:
251	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
252	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
253

```text
31:| 2026-05-29 | Patch the UDPHS device driver to arm DMA for queued IRPs in completion ISRs. New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
186:**Phototransistor placement note (clarified this session).** The fretboard sensors sit *upstream* of the strike line, at roughly the same vertical position as cv_marvin_v1's hold sense line. So the cv detector's `pressed_mask` aligns instantaneously with each fretboard ADC sample at the same moment in time — no need to time-shift labels backward. The downstream actuator (timing pipeline) owns sensor→strike-line propagation as a fixed deterministic delay. Edge-AI model's job is therefore just per-fret presence detection: "is a note at my sensor right now?" — five independent binary classifiers.

1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	The firmware deliberately contains **no game logic** — it only scans
13	ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks.
14	
15	## Hardware
16	
17	### Target
18	
19	| Spec | Value |
20	|------|-------|
21	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
22	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
23	| Clock | 24 MHz |
24	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
25	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
26	
27	### Pin Map
28	
29	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
30	
31	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
32	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
33	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
34	presence.
35	
36	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
37	|---------|-----------|-----|
38	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
39	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
40	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
41	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
42	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
43	
44	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
45	
46	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
47	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
48	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
49	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
50	
51	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
52	|----------|-----|---------|
53	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
54	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
55	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
56	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
57	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
58	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
59	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
60	
61	#### UART (SERCOM1)
62	
63	| Function | Pin |
64	|----------|-----|
65	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
66	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
67	
68	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
69	
70	## Software Architecture
71	
72	### Processing Loop
73	
74	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
75	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
76	timer ISR:
77	
78	```
79	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
80	    |
81	    v
82	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
83	    |
84	    v
85	data_stream_send()       12-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
86	    |
87	    v
88	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
89	```
90	
91	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
92	
93	### Module Descriptions
94	
95	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
96	
97	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
98	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
99	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
100	
101	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
102	the firmware:
103	
104	```
105	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
106	```
107	
108	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
109	
110	Emits one 12-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
111	
112	| Offset | Size | Field |
113	|-------:|-----:|-------|
114	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
115	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
116	| 3 | 2 | red |
117	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
118	| 7 | 2 | blue |
119	| 9 | 2 | orange |
120	| 11 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
121	
122	The frame is dropped silently if the TX free-buffer count is below the
123	frame size. At 240 Hz this is 2 880 B/s — well within the 50 000 B/s
124	budget at 500 000 baud.
125	
126	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
127	
128	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
129	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
130	
131	| Bit | Output |
132	|----:|--------|
133	| 0 | Green fret |
134	| 1 | Red fret |
135	| 2 | Yellow fret |
136	| 3 | Blue fret |
137	| 4 | Orange fret |
138	| 5 | Strum down |
139	| 6 | Strum up |
140	
141	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
142	
143	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
144	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
145	the same tick are coalesced away.
146	
147	## Tools
148	
149	### Host-side data-stream monitor
150	
151	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
152	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
153	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
154	
155	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
156	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
157	needed:
158	
159	```
160	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
161	# or, equivalently:
162	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
163	```
164	
165	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
166	
167	## Build System
168	
169	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
170	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
171	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
172	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
173	
174	## File Map
175	
176	| File | Purpose |
177	|------|---------|
178	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
179	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
180	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
181	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
182	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
183	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
184	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
185	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
186
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
    configASSERT(bus != NULL);

    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");

    for (;;)
    {
        detector_state_t state;
        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
        {
            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
            {
                continue;
            }
            process_frame(&state);
        }
        else
        {
            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
        }
    }
}

void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void)
```

62	/* Signaled from cdc_event_handler (ISR context) when a control-pipe

87	 * stamps. SYS_TIME_Counter64Get is ISR-safe (a register read; same
88	 * thing PerfLog's hdr_fill does from ISR context). */
89	static volatile int32_t  s_last_ack_result;
90	static volatile uint64_t s_last_ack_ts_counter;

103	static inline USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT arm_rx_read(USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle)
104	{
105	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th;
106	    return USB_HOST_CDC_Read(handle, &th, s_rx_buf, sizeof(s_rx_buf));

108	
109	static USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE cdc_event_handler(USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
110	                                                    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT event,
111	                                                    void *eventData,
112	                                                    uintptr_t context)
113	{
114	    (void)context;
115	
116	    switch (event)
117	    {
118	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
119	        {
120	            const USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE_DATA *d = eventData;
121	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
122	            if (d->result == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS && d->length > 0u)
123	            {
124	                (void)xStreamBufferSendFromISR(s_rx_stream, s_rx_buf,
125	                                               d->length, &hpw);
126	            }
127	            /* Re-arm immediately. If this fails (e.g. detach mid-read) the
128	             * detach event will reset state — drop silently here. */
129	            (void)arm_rx_read(handle);
130	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
131	            break;
132	        }
133	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
134	        {
135	            const USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE_DATA *d = eventData;
136	            s_last_write_result    = d->result;
137	            s_last_ack_result      = (int32_t)d->result;
138	            s_last_ack_ts_counter  = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
139	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
140	            PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE, 0u,
141	                                     (uint32_t)d->result, &hpw);
142	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
143	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
144	            break;
145	        }
146	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE:
147	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE:
148	        {
149	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
150	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_ctrl_done, &hpw);
151	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
152	            break;
153	        }
154	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_DEVICE_DETACHED:
155	        {
156	            s_connected = false;
157	            /* Wake any pending writer so it observes the detach instead
158	             * of waiting out the timeout. */
159	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
160	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
161	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
162	            break;
163	        }
164	        default:
165	            break;
166	    }
167	    return USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONE_NONE;
168	}

170	static void cdc_attach_handler(USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ obj, uintptr_t context)
171	{
172	    (void)context;
173	    /* Hand the object to the link task; opening the device must happen
174	     * outside the host stack callback. */
175	    s_cdc_obj_pending = obj;
176	    s_cdc_obj_valid   = true;
177	}
178	
179	static void close_cdc(void)
180	{
181	    if (s_cdc_handle != USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
182	    {
183	        USB_HOST_CDC_Close(s_cdc_handle);
184	        s_cdc_handle = USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID;
185	    }
186	    s_connected = false;
187	}
188	
189	static bool open_cdc(USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ obj)
190	{
191	    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE h = USB_HOST_CDC_Open(obj);
192	    if (h == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID) { return false; }
193	
194	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_EventHandlerSet(h, cdc_event_handler, 0u) != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
195	    {
196	        USB_HOST_CDC_Close(h);
197	        return false;
198	    }
199	
200	    static USB_CDC_LINE_CODING line_coding =
201	    {
202	        .dwDTERate   = FBL_BAUDRATE,
203	        .bCharFormat = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_STOP_1_BIT,
204	        .bParityType = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_PARITY_NONE,
205	        .bDataBits   = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_DATA_8_BIT,
206	    };
207	    USB_HOST_CDC_REQUEST_HANDLE rh;
208	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
209	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_LineCodingSet(h, &rh, &line_coding) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
210	    {
211	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
212	    }
213	
214	    /* Some EDBG-CDC firmwares hold the bridge UART idle until the host
215	     * raises DTR. Assert DTR + carrier so the bridge actually drives
216	     * bytes out to the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 RX. */
217	    static USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE cls = { .dtr = 1u, .carrier = 1u };
218	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
219	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet(h, &rh, &cls) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
220	    {
221	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
222	    }
223	
224	    s_cdc_handle = h;
225	    s_connected  = true;
226	
227	    /* Drop any stale bytes left from a previous attach so the parser
228	     * doesn't open mid-frame. Then arm the first Read; the READ_COMPLETE
229	     * handler keeps re-arming itself from then on. */
230	    (void)xStreamBufferReset(s_rx_stream);
231	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT rr = arm_rx_read(h);
232	    if (rr != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
233	    {
234	        LOG_WARN("FBL: initial RX arm rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)rr);
235	    }
236	    LOG_DEBUG("FBL: initial RX arm r=%d\r\n", (int)rr);
237	
238	    LOG_INFO("FBL: CDC device attached, handle opened\r\n");
239	    return true;
240	}
241	
242	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
243	{
244	    if (!s_connected) { return false; }
245	
246	    static uint8_t tx_byte;
247	    tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
248	
249	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
250	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);
251	
252	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th;
253	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT r = USB_HOST_CDC_Write(s_cdc_handle, &th, &tx_byte, 1u);
254	    if (r != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
255	    {
256	        LOG_WARN("FBL: CDC_Write rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)r);
257	        return false;
258	    }
259	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
260	
261	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
262	    {
263	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write timeout, marking detached\r\n");
264	        close_cdc();
265	        return false;
266	    }
267	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
268	    {
269	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write completion err=%d\r\n", (int)s_last_write_result);
270	        return false;
271	    }
272	    s_last_sent_byte = tx_byte;
273	    return true;
274	}
275	
276	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
277	{
278	    (void)param;
279	
280	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
281	
282	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
283	
284	    for (;;)
285	    {
286	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
287	        {
288	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;
289	            (void)open_cdc(s_cdc_obj_pending);
290	        }
291	
292	        uint8_t mask;
293	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
294	        {
295	            last_mask = mask;
296	        }
297	        else
298	        {
299	            mask = last_mask;
300	        }
301	
302	        if (s_connected)
303	        {
304	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
305	        }
306	    }
307	}
308	
309	/* Pull bytes off the RX stream buffer and emit one PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW
310	 * per parsed 12-byte frame. Resync logic mirrors tools/ds_monitor.py: a
311	 * frame is valid only when buf[0]==0x03 AND buf[11]==0xFC; otherwise drop
312	 * the leading byte and retry alignment. The FSM-free buffered approach is
313	 * easier to reason about than a state machine and the frame is short. */
314	static void fretboard_rx_task(void *param)
315	{
316	    (void)param;
317	
318	    uint8_t  frame[DS_FRAME_LEN];
319	    size_t   filled = 0u;
320	    uint32_t parsed = 0u;
321	    uint32_t skipped_bytes = 0u;
322	
323	    for (;;)
324	    {
325	        size_t want = DS_FRAME_LEN - filled;
326	        size_t got  = xStreamBufferReceive(s_rx_stream, &frame[filled],
327	                                           want, portMAX_DELAY);
328	        if (got == 0u) { continue; }
329	        filled += got;
330	        if (filled < DS_FRAME_LEN) { continue; }
331	
332	        if (frame[0] != DS_START_BYTE || frame[DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u] != DS_END_BYTE)
333	        {
334	            /* Misaligned: drop one byte and shift, then loop to refill. */
335	            memmove(&frame[0], &frame[1], DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u);
336	            filled = DS_FRAME_LEN - 1u;
337	            skipped_bytes++;
338	            continue;
339	        }
340	
341	        uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT];
342	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
343	        {
344	            adc[i] = (uint16_t)frame[1u + i * 2u]
345	                   | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)frame[2u + i * 2u] << 8);
346	        }
347	
348	        Video_FrameInfo info;
349	        Video_GetFrameInfo(&info);
350	        PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(adc, info.frame_count);
351	
352	        parsed++;
353	        if (parsed == 1u || (parsed % 240u) == 0u)
354	        {
355	            LOG_DEBUG("FBL: rx parsed=%u skipped=%u G=%u R=%u Y=%u B=%u O=%u\r\n",
356	                      (unsigned)parsed, (unsigned)skipped_bytes,
357	                      (unsigned)adc[0], (unsigned)adc[1], (unsigned)adc[2],
358	                      (unsigned)adc[3], (unsigned)adc[4]);
359	        }
360	
361	        filled = 0u;
362	    }
363	}

365	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
366	{
367	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
368	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
369	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
370	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
371	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
372	
373	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
374	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
375	
376	    s_ctrl_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_ctrl_done_buf);
377	    configASSERT(s_ctrl_done != NULL);
378	
379	    /* Storage array is FBL_RX_STREAM_BYTES + 1 per FreeRTOS — the +1 byte is
380	     * used by the buffer impl, not application data. Pass the *application*
381	     * size, not the storage size, as xBufferSizeBytes. */
382	    s_rx_stream = xStreamBufferCreateStatic(FBL_RX_STREAM_BYTES, 1u,
383	                                            s_rx_stream_storage,
384	                                            &s_rx_stream_buf);
385	    configASSERT(s_rx_stream != NULL);
386	
387	    /* Register the CDC attach listener before the bus is enabled — the host
388	     * stack only matches a class driver if its attach handler is in place
389	     * when enumeration completes. App-level USB_HOST_BusEnable runs right
390	     * after this init returns. */
391	    (void)USB_HOST_CDC_AttachEventHandlerSet(cdc_attach_handler, 0u);
392	
393	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
394	                                       "FretLink",
395	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
396	                                       NULL,
397	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
398	                                       s_task_stack,
399	                                       &s_task_tcb);
400	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
401	
402	    TaskHandle_t hr = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_rx_task,
403	                                        "FretRx",
404	                                        FBL_RX_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
405	                                        NULL,
406	                                        FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
407	                                        s_rx_task_stack,
408	                                        &s_rx_task_tcb);
409	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX, hr);
410	}

412	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
413	{
414	    return s_connected;
415	}
416	
417	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
418	{
419	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
420	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK);
421	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
422	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
423	     * stale chord state. */
424	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
425	
426	    uint8_t strum_dir = 0u;
427	    if      (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN) { strum_dir = 1u; }
428	    else if (v & TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP)   { strum_dir = 2u; }
429	
430	    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
431	                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
432	}

    End-to-end pipeline from a marvin-perf capture to a labelled CSV ready
    for import into MPLAB Machine Learning Development Suite / SensiML
    Data Capture Lab. v0 produces five independent binary classifiers
    (one per fret), label = cv_marvin_v1 pressed_mask, sensors = fretboard
    phototransistors at the upstream sense line.
    
    Tool (tools/marvin-perf):
    - New `marvin-perf export-ml <capture> --out <csv>` subcommand. Streams
      the capture, walks records once with a latest-detector cursor, emits
      one row per FRETBOARD_RAW with timestamp + 5 ADC + 5 binary labels.
      Schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset; first
      row's timestamp is 0.0 to match the "elapsed since logging started"
      convention.
    - Loud non-zero exit + warning when the export emits no detector records
      or no rows — surfaces the easy-to-miss "I forgot to enable a type"
      failure mode that previously produced a structurally-valid but
      training-useless CSV.
    - 8 new tests in test_export_sensiml_csv.py cover schema, row count,
      ADC passthrough, label step-function, timestamp arithmetic, strict
      vs non-strict pre-detector handling, and the missing-SESSION error.
    
    Web recorder (tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py):
    - Cache the framed bytes of the most-recent SESSION and DETECTOR_CONFIG
      records in `_State.prepend_framed`. On record_start, prepend them to
      the new bin so it's self-contained from byte 0 even when recording
      starts mid-session — without this, every web-mode recording missed
      SESSION (one-shot per sink-attach) and the exporter couldn't recover
      timer_freq_hz.
    
    Firmware (firmware/marvin):
    - Wire PerfLog_EmitDetector into cv_marvin_v1's detect_frame. The
      function had been defined and declared but never called: cv was
      building detector_state_t and posting it to the actuator bus
      (game played correctly) without mirroring to perf-log. This is why
      the first hardware export run produced 0 DETECTOR records despite
      bit 3 being set in the firmware mask.
    
    Journal entries cover all three fixes; verification described in
    docs/journal.md session-log.

## Edge AI Timing Pipeline Report

### 1. CV Detector: `cv_marvin_v1` Implementation & Output

**Location:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c` + `.h`

**Output:** `detector_state_t` (spec §4.2.3) — fixed 28-byte records with:
- `frame_epoch` (32-bit sync token)
- `detector_id` (0 = cv_marvin_v1)
- Five fret entries: `pressed` (binary), `confidence` (0–65535, edge signal), `raw_value` (0–65535, hold brightness)

**Detection Timeline:** Sensors sit **upstream of strike line** at hold-sense height. Two per-fret channels sample BGR patches (5×5):
- **(hx, hy)** — brightness sensor: `pressed = brightness > 100` (CV_HOLD_THRESH), hysteresis release at 78% × threshold (cv_marvin_v1.c:30–31)
- **(ex, ey)** — color-filtered edge sensor: detects rising-edge transients (edge > 25 threshold). Pressed-mask is the direct binary state at sample time (no predictive detection).

**Sensor Coordinates** (720×480 native space, Wii):
```
GREEN:  (280, 311)    RED:    (317, 311)    YELLOW: (355, 311)
BLUE:   (393, 311)    ORANGE: (430, 311)
```

**Latency:** ≤16.7 ms (one frame @ 60 Hz). Detector state immediately reflects the *current* pixel values above the strike line—notes are detected when they appear at sensor position, not when they reach strike line later. The downstream timing pipeline compensates with a 220 ms delay constant (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS`).

---

### 2. Timing Pipeline: Detector→Command Path

**Location:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c` + `.h`

**Flow:**
1. `timing_pipeline_task` consumes `detector_state_t` from `Detector_BusQueue()` (M3, working).
2. **Chord window (30 ms):** Accumulates pressing edges. On window close, computes two scheduled events:
   - **Note assert:** `now + 220 ms (STRUM_DELAY_MS) − 50 ms (FRET_EARLY_MS)` = `now + 170 ms` 
   - **Strum fire:** `now + 220 ms` 
3. Events land in two **FIFO queues** (32 entries each, `timing_pipeline.c:50–53`):
   - `s_note_q[]` → fret bitmask + `assert_at_ms`
   - `s_strum_q[]` → fret bitmask + `strum_at_ms`
4. Background tick (5 ms intervals) fires notes/strums when deadlines expire.
5. Commands sent via `FretboardLink_Send()` as 1-byte bitmask (bits 0–4 = frets, bits 5–6 = strum direction).

**Arbitration:** Two producers exist (timing_pipeline + manual_control). Mode arbitration lives above: `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool)` gates the `FretboardLink_Send()` call; internal state still advances. Default: timing_pipeline enabled during gameplay.

---

### 3. Phototransistor Sensing

**Location:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`; PCB: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`

**Five channels, 240 Hz scan rate, 12-bit ADC (0–4095, lower=brighter):**
- Physically positioned **upstream (above) the strike line**, at roughly the same vertical lane as cv_marvin_v1's brightness sensor. 
- **Alignment:** cv_marvin_v1's pressed_mask and fretboard ADC samples align instantaneously—no time-shift needed for training labels (journal 2026-06-02).
- **Frame format:** 12 bytes little-endian: `[0x03, green_u16, red_u16, yellow_u16, blue_u16, orange_u16, 0xFC]` emitted every 4.17 ms.

---

### 4. ADC Stream: Packet Format & Reception

**Fretboard → Marvin:** USB CDC host (500 000 baud, EDBG bridge) at 240 Hz = 2,880 B/s.

**Marvin ingestion:** 
- `fretboard_link.c`: continuously-rearmed `USB_HOST_CDC_Read()` + sibling `fretboard_rx_task` (priority 5, 512-byte stream buffer).
- Parses `0x03…0xFC` frames, emits `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` (28 B) with `frame_epoch` tag (perf_log v2 onward).
- Resync logic: if framing breaks, scans for next `0x03` boundary.

**Current recording:** Until SD persistence (M4) lands, all ADC lives in perf-log USB CDC export only (~6.7 KB/s @ 240 Hz).

---

### 5. ML Training Export: `marvin-perf export-ml`

**Location:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py`

**Labeling Alignment:**
- Consumes perf-log capture (FRETBOARD_RAW + DETECTOR records).
- One CSV row per fretboard ADC sample (~240 Hz).
- Labels broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`: one cv frame ≈ 4 fretboard rows, all share the same cv_marvin_v1 `pressed_mask`.
- **SensiML CSV schema:** `timestamp, ph_green..ph_orange, label_green..label_orange` (11 columns, 0.0 start time, elapsed seconds).

**Exported:**
- `timestamp`: seconds since SESSION (firmware timer base).
- `ph_*`: raw 12-bit ADC, no normalization (SensiML normalizes in training).
- `label_*`: five binary classifiers (one per fret) from cv detector's pressed state.

**Edge case:** FretboardRaw before any Detector → emitted with all labels=0 (or dropped with `--strict`).

---

### 6. Strum Timing in Current Pipeline

**When strum fires:** `timing_pipeline.c:199–200` — scheduled at `now + 220 ms` (STRUM_DELAY_MS).

**Strum-fired signal:** Yes, recorded in perf-log via `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` (v3 schema, 2026-06-01). Carries `intended_mask`, `asserted_mask`, `producer_id`, and `strum_dir` each time a bitmask publishes—including strum bits 5–6.

**No sensor feedback yet:** Strum assert is command-driven (open-drain GPIO to Wii controller), no readback. Timing is deterministic relative to detector frame epoch once the chord window closes.

---

**Summary:** Pipeline is end-to-end working (M1–M3 complete). CV detects notes upstream; timing adds 220 ms compensating delay; ADC labels align frame-epoch-wise with cv ground truth for Edge-AI training (export-ml ready as of 2026-06-02).

commit 2faab1cb515d892f0701c292e6cf497eea8cb84c
Author: Greg Mrozek <greg.mrozek@microchip.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 2 14:50:48 2026 -0500

    marvin: capture fretboard ADC stream into perf-log
    
    Step 1 of the Edge-AI training-dataset workstream: route the fretboard's
    240 Hz raw ADC frames through marvin's perf-log so an offline tool can
    join them with cv_marvin_v1's per-frame detector output. CV detector =
    ground-truth label; fretboard sensors = the input the future Edge-AI
    MCU would see.
    
    Wire schema (additive, no PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION bump):
    - PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW = 0x0B (28 B: hdr + 5×u16 ADC + reserved)
    - PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX = 17 (HWM/RUNTIME slot for the new task)
    - PERF_STAGE_FBL_READ_COMPLETE = 0x42 (per-Read STAMP, peer of
      CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE; aux = (result << 24) | length)
    
    Firmware:
    - New PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw producer mirrors EmitDetector shape;
      default-disabled at boot like the other high-rate types.
    - fretboard_link.c gains the RX path it never had: a 512 B static stream
      buffer, a READ_COMPLETE handler that pushes bytes via
      xStreamBufferSendFromISR and re-arms the read, plus first-arm at the
      end of open_cdc(). New sibling fretboard_rx_task (priority 5, 512-word
      stack) parses the 0x03..0xFC framed 12-byte payload, looks up the
      current frame_count via Video_GetFrameInfo, and emits one record per
      parsed frame.
    
    Host (tools/marvin-perf):
    - records.py / decode.py: FretboardRaw dataclass + dispatch entry,
      RecordType.FRETBOARD_RAW, TaskId.FRETBOARD_RX, Stage.FBL_READ_COMPLETE.
    - web UI: FRETBOARD_RAW checkbox in the Types panel (default-off, like
      STRIP); restored IDLE/OTHER to the per-task RTOS table (the totals
      header above the table stays for at-a-glance) since they're useful
      directly in workload-row comparisons.
    
    Verified end-to-end on hardware: 240 frames/s with skipped=0, sensible
    ADC values (~3800-3970/4095, "no note present"). 74/74 host pytests
    still pass. Diagnostic LOG_DEBUG lines in fretboard_rx_task off by
    default; enable via log_set_level(LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG).
    
    Out of scope (deliberate): the adc_fretboard detector that publishes
    onto the detector-state bus (spec §4.2, M2; bus slot
    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1 already reserved); offline join/export tool
    that turns a perf-log capture into a training-friendly format.
