1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ USB CDC host (cmds)      │ USB CDC host (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.
45	
46	## 3. Subproject specs (where detail lives)
47	
48	| Subproject | Spec | Journal |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| marvin | [`firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) | [`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) |
51	| fretboard | [`firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) | — |
52	| fret-tuner | [`tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md) | — |
53	| marvin-perf | [`tools/marvin-perf/`](tools/marvin-perf/) — perf-log decoder + live/offline web viewer | — |
54	
55	marvin's spec also has deeper-dive documents for its capture and display paths ([`capture_pipeline.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md), [`display_path.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md)).
56	
57	## 4. Repository map
58	
59	```
60	guitar-pic/
61	├── README.md                    # short landing page
62	├── SPEC.md                      # this document
63	├── CLAUDE.md                    # workflow rules for Claude Code sessions
64	├── firmware/
65	│   ├── marvin/                  # SAM9X75 host firmware
66	│   ├── fretboard/               # PIC32CM6408 sensor/actuator MCU firmware
67	│   └── sam9x75_curiosity_emirror/   # Microchip reference project (template only)
68	├── tools/
69	│   ├── fret-tuner/              # Python dev/calibration tool
70	│   └── marvin-perf/             # marvin perf-log decoder + web viewer
71	├── hardware/
72	│   ├── actuators/               # voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid design + test protocols
73	│   ├── 3d-models/               # OpenSCAD + STL for printed actuator parts
74	│   ├── Sensor-LCD5/             # KiCad project for fretboard sensor/actuator PCB
75	│   └── kicad/                   # shared symbol/footprint libraries
76	└── docs/
77	    ├── SAM9X7-Series-Data-Sheet-DS60001813.pdf
78	    └── archive/                 # historical docs from the original PC/Elgato/PS2 architecture
79	```
80	
81	## 5. Hardware platforms (high-level)
82	
83	| Component | Role | Where to look |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| SAM9X75 Curiosity | marvin host | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) |
86	| Waveshare HDMI→CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) | HDMI bridge into marvin | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md), [capture pipeline](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md) |
87	| 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch | marvin operator UI surface | [marvin display path](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md) |
88	| Sensor/actuator PCB (Sensor-LCD5) | fretboard board: 5 phototransistors + GPIO out | [`hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`](hardware/Sensor-LCD5/) |
89	| PIC32CM6408PL10048 | fretboard MCU | [fretboard spec](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
90	| Actuator mechanism (TBD: voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) | physical fret + strum drive | [`hardware/actuators/`](hardware/actuators/) and [`hardware/3d-models/`](hardware/3d-models/) |
91	| ElectronWarp | component → HDMI converter for Wii | external commercial part |
92	
93	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
94	
95	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
96	
97	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
98	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
99	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
100	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
```
</details></tool-use>

2

4	
5	import csv
6	from pathlib import Path
7	
8	import pytest
9	
10	from marvin_perf.capture import BIN_NAME, CaptureSource, finalize_capture_dir, init_capture_dir
11	from marvin_perf.exporters.sensiml_csv import (
12	    ExportError,
13	    export_sensiml_csv,
14	)

17	    build_detector_payload,
18	    build_fretboard_raw_payload,
19	    wrap_frame,
20	)
21	
22	
23	_TIMER_HZ = 1_000_000  # 1 MHz → ts_counter == microseconds (easy arithmetic)
24	_TS_PER_FRAME = _TIMER_HZ // 60  # one video frame at 60 Hz
25	_TS_PER_FRETBOARD = _TIMER_HZ // 240  # one fretboard tick at 240 Hz
26	
27	
28	def _write_capture(tmp_path: Path, payloads: list[bytes]) -> Path:
29	    cap_dir = init_capture_dir(tmp_path / "cap")
30	    bin_path = cap_dir / BIN_NAME
31	    with bin_path.open("wb") as fh:
32	        for p in payloads:
33	            fh.write(wrap_frame(p))
34	    finalize_capture_dir(cap_dir, source=CaptureSource(kind="file", file=str(bin_path)))
35	    return cap_dir
36	
37	
38	def _build_session_first(ts_counter: int = 0) -> bytes:
39	    """SESSION record body builder doesn't expose ts_counter; patch it in."""
40	    import struct
41	    from marvin_perf.records import PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, RecordType, Session
42	
43	    hdr = struct.pack(
44	        "<HBBIQ", PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, int(RecordType.SESSION), 0, 0, ts_counter
45	    )
46	    body = Session._BODY.pack(_TIMER_HZ, 3, 0, 0, 0)
47	    return hdr + body
48	
49	
50	def _make_capture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
51	    """A small synthetic capture covering the join paths.
52	
53	    Layout (timer_freq_hz=1 MHz so each ts_counter unit = 1 µs):
54	      SESSION                                                ts=0
55	      DETECTOR  epoch=1  pressed=0b00000  (no presses)       ts=10_000
56	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=1  adc=(100,200,...)          ts=10_000 + 0..3 ticks
57	      DETECTOR  epoch=2  pressed=0b00001  (green pressed)    ts=10_000 + 1 frame
58	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=2  adc=(50,...)               ts=...
59	      DETECTOR  epoch=3  pressed=0b00101  (green+yellow)     ts=...
60	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=3  adc=(40,...)               ts=...
61	
62	    First detector record arrives BEFORE the first fretboard record so the
63	    "skipped pre-detector" path is covered by a separate test.
64	    """
65	    payloads: list[bytes] = [_build_session_first(ts_counter=0)]
66	
67	    base = 10_000
68	    schedule = [
69	        (1, 0b00000, (3900, 3950, 3850, 3900, 3900)),
70	        (2, 0b00001, (1200, 3940, 3840, 3890, 3890)),  # green pressed → low
71	        (3, 0b00101, (1100, 3935, 1500, 3885, 3885)),  # green + yellow
72	    ]
73	    for i, (epoch, pressed, adc) in enumerate(schedule):
74	        det_ts = base + i * _TS_PER_FRAME
75	        payloads.append(
76	            build_detector_payload(
77	                frame_epoch=epoch,
78	                pressed_mask=pressed,
79	                edge_active_mask=0,
80	            )
81	        )
82	        for k in range(4):
83	            fb_ts = det_ts + k * _TS_PER_FRETBOARD
84	            payloads.append(
85	                build_fretboard_raw_payload(
86	                    frame_epoch=epoch, ts_counter=fb_ts, adc=adc
87	                )
88	            )
89	
90	    return _write_capture(tmp_path, payloads)
91	
92	
93	def _read_csv(path: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
94	    with path.open() as fh:
95	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
96	        rows = list(reader)
97	    return rows[0], rows[1:]

Excellent. Now let me create a summary report with my findings:

## Summary Report: Timing Alignment Between CV Detector & Fretboard Phototransistors

**Misalignment Root Cause**: The sensors sample at different spatial regions of the game screen, creating a **fundamental temporal offset** that the current perf-log + SensiML CSV pipeline does not account for.

---

### 1. **Phototransistor Physical Placement** (Upstream of Strike)

**Location**: Fretboard PCB samples at the **sensing line** — above the strike-line region where notes are played.

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md:31-34*
- Five phototransistors positioned **above the TV strike line**
- Each produces analog voltage that drops when a note passes
- ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); **lower values = note present**

---

### 2. **CV Detector ROI: Two Distinct Regions**

The cv_marvin_v1 detector samples at **two screen rows**, both above the strike:

**A. Sensing strip** (y=311 in 720×480 frame space):  
*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:36-51*
- Brightness (hold) sensor: `s_sensor_coords[i].hy = 311` for all 5 frets
- Color-filtered edge sensor: `s_sensor_coords[i].ey = 311` for all 5 frets
- Comment states: "both above the strike line"

**B. Strike strip** (y=212 in frame space):  
*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:395-404*
```c
PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
                           (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
                           265u, 300, 185u, 32u);  // y=265 base, height=32u
PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
                           (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
                           212u, 395u, 290u, 32u);  // y=212 base, height=32u
```
- "Sensing strip centers on the sensor row (y=311); strike strip is below the sensors at the strum trigger zone"
- **Strike strip is sampled for visualization only** — not used in detection logic (cv_marvin_v1 only reads y=311)

---

### 3. **Frame_Epoch Alignment: Detector vs. ADC Samples**

Both record `frame_epoch` (video frame count), but **at different rates**, creating a many-to-one mapping:

| Component | Rate | Record Type | Frame Epoch | Timestamp |
|-----------|------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| CV Detector | 60 Hz (~16.7 ms) | PERF_REC_DETECTOR | `frame.frame_count` | `xTaskGetTickCount() * US_PER_TICK` |
| Fretboard ADC | 240 Hz (~4.17 ms) | PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW | `Video_GetFrameInfo().frame_count` (same as CV) | `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()` (ISR) |

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:156-157*  
*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:348-350*

**Behavior**: Approximately **4 consecutive FRETBOARD_RAW records** carry the **same frame_epoch** as one DETECTOR record (240 ÷ 60 = 4).

---

### 4. **SensiML CSV Export: Label Propagation Method**

The exporter performs a **step-function forward-fill** of detector labels across fretboard samples:

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py:100-124*

```python
if isinstance(rec, Detector):
    last_detector = rec
    n_detector_records += 1
    continue

if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
    # ... timestamp calc ...
    pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
    row = [
        f"{t_s:.6f}",
        rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
        (pressed >> 0) & 1,  # Extract bit for each fret
        (pressed >> 1) & 1,
        ...
    ]
    writer.writerow(row)
```

**CSV Schema** (11 columns):
- `timestamp` — seconds since SESSION record
- `ph_green` ... `ph_orange` — 5× ADC values (0–4095, lower = note)
- `label_green` ... `label_orange` — 5× binary fret-pressed flags (from DETECTOR.pressed_mask)

**Example (test case)** from `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_export_sensiml_csv.py:69-71`:
- Epoch 1: `pressed=0b00000` → all labels = 0 → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 0,0,0,0,0]`
- Epoch 2: `pressed=0b00001` (green) → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 1,0,0,0,0]`
- Epoch 3: `pressed=0b00101` (green + yellow) → 4 CSV rows with `[ADC, 1,0,1,0,0]`

---

### 5. **Strum Timing: Commands vs. Firings (Not Currently Recorded)**

The current perf-log captures **when marvin emits button-press commands**, not **when fretboard physically asserts strum GPIO**:

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:417-432*

```c
void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask, uint8_t producer_id)
{
    // ... queue mask ...
    PerfLog_EmitActuator(v, s_last_sent_byte, strum_dir, producer_id,
                         s_last_ack_result, s_last_ack_ts_counter);
}
```

**PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record** (*perf_log_records.h:330-343*):
- `intended_mask` — the command being sent
- `asserted_mask` — last successfully transmitted byte (tracked as `s_last_sent_byte`)
- `strum_dir` — direction (0=none, 1=down, 2=up)
- `producer_id` — TIMING (pipeline) or others
- `last_ack_result` — USB CDC result
- `last_ack_ts_counter` — when the CDC write completed

**Critical gap**: No record of **when the fretboard GPIO actually fires** or **when the strum solenoid energizes**. The CSV exporter ignores PERF_REC_ACTUATOR entirely — **strum timing is not a training label or input feature**.

*Source: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py:1-19*: Comment states "label = cv_marvin_v1 pressed_mask" — no mention of strum data.

---

### 6. **The Misalignment Problem: Spatial Offset**

Notes scroll down the screen from top to bottom. The detector at y=311 and the physical fretboard phototransistors see the same note at **different times**:

1. Note appears high on screen → fretboard ADC sees it (note approaching y=311)
2. ~50–100 ms later → CV detector at y=311 sees it
3. ~100–150 ms later → Strike line (y~450) reached; strum should fire

**Current CSV export aligns by frame_epoch only**, which compresses 4.17 ms of ADC data into a single detector label. **No sub-frame temporal correction** is applied.

---

### 7. **What Fields Exist Today vs. Missing**

| Aspect | Recorded | Missing |
|--------|----------|---------|
| CV detector (y=311) output per frame | ✓ PERF_REC_DETECTOR (60 Hz) | Sub-frame timing within detector frame |
| Fretboard ADC raw samples | ✓ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (240 Hz) | ADC sample jitter / actual sample timestamps |
| Frame alignment token | ✓ `frame_epoch` (common) | Spatial offset between sensor regions |
| Strum command intent | ✓ PERF_REC_ACTUATOR | Strum GPIO firing time (fretboard-side) |
| Strum result (ACK) | ✓ USB CDC write-complete | Physical strum solenoid energization |
| Strike-line occupancy | ~ PERF_STRIP_STRIKE (visualization only) | Unused in detection; no binary label |
| Label propagation | ✓ Forward-fill (SensiML CSV) | Temporal interpolation for note descent |

---

### Bottom Line

**The misalignment is a spatial causality issue**: the fretboard phototransistors (above strike, at unknown y) detect notes before the cv_detector (y=311) and way before the strike line. The SensiML CSV exporter currently:
- Assigns a **single binary label per 4-sample ADC window** (step function forward-fill)
- Does **not model the note-descent trajectory** or the ~50–150 ms offset between detection regions
- Does **not include strum timing** as a label or feature

For improved ML training, you'd need either:
1. **Temporal shift correction**: Measure or estimate the pixel-scroll rate and offset ADC labels backward in time
2. **Spatial ROI labels**: Add strikes at y=212 (strum line) as a secondary binary label
3. **Strum event capture**: Log fretboard GPIO assertions or solenoid current from the fretboard MCU

EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). 1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	The firmware deliberately contains **no game logic** — it only scans
13	ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks.
14	
15	## Hardware
16	
17	### Target
18	
19	| Spec | Value |
20	|------|-------|
21	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
22	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
23	| Clock | 24 MHz |
24	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
25	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
26	
27	### Pin Map
28	
29	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
30	
31	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
32	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
33	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
34	presence.
35	
36	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
37	|---------|-----------|-----|
38	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
39	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
40	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
41	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
42	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
43	
44	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
45	
46	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
47	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
48	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
49	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
50	
51	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
52	|----------|-----|---------|
53	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
54	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
55	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
56	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
57	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
58	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
59	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
60	
61	#### UART (SERCOM1)
62	
63	| Function | Pin |
64	|----------|-----|
65	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
66	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
67	
68	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
69	
70	## Software Architecture
71	
72	### Processing Loop
73	
74	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
75	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
76	timer ISR:
77	
78	```
79	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
80	    |
81	    v
82	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
83	    |
84	    v
85	data_stream_send()       12-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
86	    |
87	    v
88	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
89	```
90	
91	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
92	
93	### Module Descriptions
94	
95	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
96	
97	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
98	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
99	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
100	
101	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
102	the firmware:
103	
104	```
105	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
106	```
107	
108	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
109	
110	Emits one 12-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
111	
112	| Offset | Size | Field |
113	|-------:|-----:|-------|
114	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
115	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
116	| 3 | 2 | red |
117	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
118	| 7 | 2 | blue |
119	| 9 | 2 | orange |
120	| 11 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
121	
122	The frame is dropped silently if the TX free-buffer count is below the
123	frame size. At 240 Hz this is 2 880 B/s — well within the 50 000 B/s
124	budget at 500 000 baud.
125	
126	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
127	
128	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
129	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
130	
131	| Bit | Output |
132	|----:|--------|
133	| 0 | Green fret |
134	| 1 | Red fret |
135	| 2 | Yellow fret |
136	| 3 | Blue fret |
137	| 4 | Orange fret |
138	| 5 | Strum down |
139	| 6 | Strum up |
140	
141	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
142	
143	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
144	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
145	the same tick are coalesced away.
146	
147	## Tools
148	
149	### Host-side data-stream monitor
150	
151	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
152	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
153	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
154	
155	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
156	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
157	needed:
158	
159	```
160	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
161	# or, equivalently:
162	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
163	```
164	
165	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
166	
167	## Build System
168	
169	MPLAB Extensions for VS Code. Project config is in
170	`.vscode/fretboard.mplab.json`. Source files are listed in the
171	`fileSets[0].files` array. MCC/Harmony-generated code lives under
172	`fretboard-mcc/` and should not be edited.
173	
174	## File Map
175	
176	| File | Purpose |
177	|------|---------|
178	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
179	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
180	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
181	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
182	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
183	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
184	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
185	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
186

1	"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.
2	
3	One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
4	ADC values plus five binary labels (one per fret), where the label comes
5	from the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask broadcast forward by
6	frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame).
7	
8	CSV schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset:
9	    timestamp,ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
10	    label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
11	
12	`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the SESSION record's ts_counter.
13	
14	Edge cases:
15	- FretboardRaw records before any Detector record are emitted with all
16	  labels = 0 by default; pass strict=True to drop them instead.
17	- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
18	  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import csv
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from pathlib import Path
26	
27	from ..capture import open_capture
28	from ..decode import decode_record
29	from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
30	from ..records import Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
31	from ..transport import FileSource
32	
33	
34	_HEADER = (
35	    "timestamp",
36	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
37	    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
38	)
39	
40	
41	class ExportError(Exception):
42	    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class ExportStats:
47	    n_rows: int
48	    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
49	    n_detector_records: int
50	    n_fretboard_records: int
51	    t_start_s: float
52	    t_end_s: float
53	    timer_freq_hz: int
54	
55	    @property
56	    def duration_s(self) -> float:
57	        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s
58	
59	
60	def export_sensiml_csv(
61	    capture_path: str | Path,
62	    out_path: str | Path,
63	    *,
64	    strict: bool = False,
65	) -> ExportStats:
66	    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.
67	
68	    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
69	    Detector record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
70	    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts
71	    before cv_marvin_v1 has produced its first frame.
72	    """
73	    capture = open_capture(capture_path)
74	
75	    session: Session | None = None
76	    last_detector: Detector | None = None
77	    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
78	    n_detector_records = 0
79	    n_fretboard_records = 0
80	    n_rows = 0
81	    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
82	    t_end_s = 0.0
83	
84	    out_path = Path(out_path)
85	    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
86	        writer = csv.writer(fh)
87	        writer.writerow(_HEADER)
88	        stats = FrameStats()
89	
90	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
91	            try:
92	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
93	            except Exception:
94	                continue
95	
96	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
97	                session = rec
98	                continue
99	
100	            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
101	                last_detector = rec
102	                n_detector_records += 1
103	                continue
104	
105	            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
106	                n_fretboard_records += 1
107	                if session is None:
108	                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
109	                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
110	                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
111	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
112	                    continue
113	                if last_detector is None and strict:
114	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
115	                    continue
116	
117	                if t_baseline is None:
118	                    t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
119	                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(
120	                    session.timer_freq_hz
121	                )
122	                t_end_s = t_s
123	
124	                pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
125	                row = [
126	                    f"{t_s:.6f}",
127	                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
128	                    (pressed >> 0) & 1,
129	                    (pressed >> 1) & 1,
130	                    (pressed >> 2) & 1,
131	                    (pressed >> 3) & 1,
132	                    (pressed >> 4) & 1,
133	                ]
134	                writer.writerow(row)
135	                n_rows += 1
136	
137	    if session is None:
138	        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
139	        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
140	        try:
141	            out_path.unlink()
142	        except FileNotFoundError:
143	            pass
144	        raise ExportError(
145	            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
146	            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
147	        )
148	
149	    return ExportStats(
150	        n_rows=n_rows,
151	        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
152	        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
153	        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
154	        t_start_s=0.0 if n_rows > 0 else 0.0,
155	        t_end_s=t_end_s,
156	        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
157	    )
158

# Plan — Edge AI design exploration

## Context

We want to design how the **edge AI** subsystem fits into the guitar-bot. The current state of the world:

- **`cv_marvin_v1`** samples a single screen row at `y=311` ("sensing line") — *above* the strike line. For each fret it emits `pressed_mask` + `confidence` + `raw_value`. ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c))
- **fretboard ADC** samples 5 phototransistors at 240 Hz that physically sit "above the TV strike line". Where exactly relative to `y=311` is unverified — it's a *different* point on the screen than CV's sensing row, and that's the spatial-mismatch the user is worried about.
- **Timing pipeline** on marvin closes a 30 ms chord window, schedules note assert at `+170 ms` and strum at `+220 ms` (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS`), and pushes a 1-byte bitmask over USB CDC to fretboard. ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c))
- **`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`** records *every* command marvin sends, with `intended_mask`, `strum_dir`, `producer_id`, ack timing — this is the marvin pipeline's *final output*, captured per-event. Currently **unused** by the SensiML exporter.
- **`sensiml_csv.py`** exports rows at the 240 Hz fretboard rate, with labels = the most-recent CV `pressed_mask` broadcast forward by `frame_epoch` (≈4 ADC rows per CV frame). Strum timing is not represented.

## The design tension Greg raised

> Labels (CV) and ADC are not in sync because they sample different points before the strike line. Trying to align them at the same point is finicky and limiting. And we're not pulling button-press / strum timing into the edge AI at all — it's only doing fret button presses.

Two distinct issues:

1. **Spatial alignment**: CV at `y=311` and the phototransistor row see the same falling note at different times. Forcing them onto the same frame-epoch creates a fixed offset that's only correct if the scroll speed is constant.
2. **Output shape too narrow**: predicting `pressed_mask` at a single moment ignores the strum decision. The downstream pipeline (chord window + +220 ms scheduler) is doing real work that the AI is being denied.

## Design space (to discuss)

I see four genuinely different shapes for the model. Each is a different bet about what the AI's job is.

### Shape A — Frame classifier (current direction, plus alignment fix)

- **Input:** the 5 ADC channels at the current sample (or a tiny window).
- **Output:** `pressed_mask` *at the same instant the photoxistors observe*.
- **Label source:** a *new* CV detector that samples the same screen row the phototransistors look at, so cv label and ADC are spatially co-located.
- **Pipeline:** classifier output replaces `cv_marvin_v1` on the bus; **timing pipeline still runs on marvin** and turns it into strums.
- Pros: small model, easy to label, contained scope.
- Cons: still doesn't pull strum timing into the AI; still requires aligning a CV row with the photoxistor row (mechanical/optical work).

### Shape B — Sequence model with CV-strike-line as oracle

- **Input:** a causal window of the 5 ADC channels (e.g. last 200–400 ms = 48–96 samples @ 240 Hz).
- **Output:** what's at the *strike line* right now (or in N ms).
- **Label source:** add a new CV detector that watches the **strike row** and emits the strike-line truth — that's the moment-of-truth, not the sensing-line precursor. Model learns the upstream→strike mapping implicitly.
- Pros: solves the spatial-mismatch problem by *not* aligning ADC with CV-sensing — it aligns ADC-history with CV-strike-truth, which has a real physical meaning.
- Cons: needs new detector code; classifier-only model still doesn't time strums.

### Shape C — Distill the whole marvin pipeline (recommended starting point)

- **Input:** causal window of 5 ADC channels + recent strum-history (~last 200 ms of own outputs, optional).
- **Output:** the byte that would go to the fretboard right now — fret bits + strum-down/up bits.
- **Label source:** **`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` resampled onto the 240 Hz ADC grid.** Marvin already records every command it emits. We use marvin as a *teacher* and let the AI learn `f(adc_window) → command_byte` end-to-end.
- Pros:
  - Sidesteps the spatial-mismatch entirely. The label is "what marvin chose to do, given the same upstream signals", not a CV intermediate.
  - **Pulls strum timing into the AI by construction** — strum bits are part of the output.
  - Marvin's reference detector + 30 ms chord window + +220 ms scheduler are all baked into the supervision signal; edge AI replicates the full behaviour in one shot.
  - Works as a clean ablation: "can a small model trained on ADC alone match marvin's commands within ±N ms?".
- Cons:
  - Inherits any bugs in marvin's pipeline (but you wanted that anyway — it's the ground truth).
  - Strum-event labels are sparse; need careful loss weighting (fret-mask is dense, strum is rare and timing-sensitive).

### Shape D — Two-head event detector

- **Input:** same as C.
- **Output head 1:** continuous `pressed_mask` (dense, smooth).
- **Output head 2:** strum event with `[time_to_strum, fret_mask_at_strum, strum_dir]` (sparse).
- **Label source:** head 1 ← marvin's pressed-track from `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` or the new strike-row CV; head 2 ← marvin's `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` strum events.
- Pros: separates the two regimes (continuous fret hold vs. discrete strum), which is closer to the underlying physics (a held note vs. a strum stroke). Better loss landscape than one head trying to do both.
- Cons: more complex to architect, more careful labeling.

## Sensors / topology questions still open

- **Will the edge AI run on fretboard (24 MHz Cortex-M0+, very tight) or a separate AI-class MCU?** This caps the window size and architecture.
- **Should the model be allowed to see strike-line CV at runtime (training oracle only) or is it ADC-only?** Pure ADC keeps the edge AI standalone; ADC + low-bandwidth strike pulse is a tiny channel that drastically simplifies the problem.
- **What sample rate does the ADC need to be at?** 240 Hz is fine for current 480p60. If we go to longer windows / higher resolution, may want 500 Hz or oversampling.

## Open questions for Greg

(Asking these next. Once answered, the plan will narrow to one shape and detail the data-pipeline changes, the new perf-log records / CV detector if any, and a model-architecture sketch.)

<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**What should the edge AI model output? This is the biggest fork in the road.**

Options:
- **Fret-press mask only (current)** - A: Per-sample pressed_mask classifier. Timing pipeline still runs upstream of the model — model only replaces the CV detector's output. Strum decisions stay outside the AI.
- **Strike-line truth** - B: Sequence model predicts what's at the strike row right now / in N ms. New CV detector at the strike line provides the oracle label. Strum timing is still scheduled by a downstream rule.
- **Full fretboard command byte (distill marvin)** - C: Model emits the same byte marvin sends to fretboard — fret bits + strum bits — supervised against PERF_REC_ACTUATOR. Pulls strum timing into the AI; sidesteps CV/ADC spatial alignment.
- **Two heads: pressed + strum events** - D: One continuous head for held-note state, one sparse head for strum events with fret-mask + direction. Closer to the physics; more complex to train.

**Where does the trained model run at inference time?**

Options:
- **Fretboard PIC32CM (24 MHz M0+)** - Tight: ~24 MHz Cortex-M0+, no FPU, kilobytes of RAM. Forces a tiny model (a few hundred params, e.g. tiny 1D-CNN or rule-distilled tree). Removes marvin from the runtime loop end-to-end.
- **A new dedicated AI MCU** - Separate MCU on its own board (or section of the fretboard PCB), receiving the ADC stream — picked for its ML accelerator (e.g. PIC32CK with Cortana, or a SAMA7 with NPU). More compute headroom; preserves marvin's role for training.
- **Marvin (SAM9X75)** - Run the model on marvin alongside cv_marvin_v1, replacing or competing with it. Lots of headroom (Cortex-A5, hundreds of MHz). Defeats the 'edge MCU AI' framing but fastest path to validate the approach before squeezing onto a small chip.
- **Undecided / want to discuss** - Defer the deployment target, design the data pipeline first.

**What inputs is the model allowed to see at inference?**

Options:
- **5 ADC channels only (pure edge)** - Phototransistor stream is the entire input. Most ambitious: model has to learn note timing from the sensor row alone. Edge AI can run with marvin off.
- **ADC + tiny strike-line pulse** - Photonsistors + a low-bandwidth signal from a separate strike-line phototransistor (or CV pulse). Drastically simplifies timing — strum-when-strike-pulse-fires becomes trivial.
- **ADC + marvin-side feature** - Model receives ADC plus a feature from marvin's CV detector (e.g. note-arrival event, scroll speed estimate). Edge AI is a co-processor, not standalone.

**Should training data come only from marvin's own play, or also from human play / synthetic?** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **Marvin self-play (distillation)** - Record marvin playing songs; ADC + emitted commands form (input, label) pairs. Easiest to collect; AI inherits marvin's decisions.
- **Human play recordings** - Human plays the guitar with phototransistors active; record ADC + ground-truth presses (from controller readback). Richer label set but needs an authoring path.
- **Synthetic (simulator)** - Generate ADC traces from a screen-scroll model + label generator. Fast to scale, but sim-to-real gap is real.


**Answer:** Full fretboard command byte (distill marvin), Fretboard PIC32CM (24 MHz M0+), 5 ADC channels only to start. We may add another channel per fret similar to cv sensing. I'm open to suggestions here though. The phototransistor placement / number / etc. is still open, Marvin self-play (distillation)

# Plan — Edge AI design (distill marvin onto fretboard)

## Context

We want to design how the **edge AI** subsystem fits into the guitar-bot. State of the world:

- **`cv_marvin_v1`** ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)) samples one screen row at `y=311` (above the strike line) and emits a `pressed_mask` per CV frame — purely a fret-press classifier, no strum semantics.
- **fretboard ADC** ([fretboard/SPEC.md](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md)) samples 5 phototransistors at 240 Hz; sensors physically sit "above the TV strike line" — but at a different (unverified) screen row than CV's `y=311`.
- **Timing pipeline** ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) closes a 30 ms chord window, schedules note assert at +170 ms and strum at +220 ms (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS`), and emits a 1-byte fret+strum bitmask to fretboard. Every byte it emits is captured as `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` (with `strum_dir`, `producer_id`, ack timing). This record type is currently **not used** by the SensiML CSV exporter — labels come from `PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask` instead.
- **`sensiml_csv.py`** ([tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py)) exports rows at 240 Hz with `pressed_mask` broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`. Strum bits aren't represented.

## Greg's concerns

1. **Spatial mismatch.** CV at `y=311` and the photoxistors look at different screen rows, so the same falling note hits each at different times. Forcing them onto the same `frame_epoch` bakes in a fixed offset that's only valid at one scroll speed.
2. **Output too narrow.** Predicting `pressed_mask` ignores the strum decision. The chord window + +220 ms scheduler is real work the AI is being denied.

## Decisions

Locked from the question round:

- **Output shape:** the full 1-byte fretboard command — 5 fret bits + strum-down + strum-up.
- **Supervision:** **distillation** against marvin's own emitted commands (`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask`), resampled onto the 240 Hz ADC grid by forward-fill between events. Marvin is the teacher; AI replicates its end-to-end behaviour.
- **Deployment target:** fretboard MCU (PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz, 32 KB RAM, no FPU). Tight, but removes marvin from the runtime loop.
- **Inference inputs:** 5 ADC channels only for v1, with optional per-fret expansion later.
- **Training corpus:** marvin self-play recordings only.

The key insight that makes shape C clean: **the spatial-alignment issue dissolves automatically.** The label is no longer a CV intermediate at a particular screen row — it is the command byte marvin chose to emit, with marvin's +220 ms strum delay already baked in. As long as the model gets a wide enough causal window of ADC, it learns whatever delay maps photo-row signal to strum command, regardless of where the photoxistors physically sit.

## Recommended architecture

### Inference shape

- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × ~60 samples = 250 ms causal window @ 240 Hz, int16. ≈600 bytes.
- **Output:** 7 binary outputs at the current time step — `[fret_g, fret_r, fret_y, fret_b, fret_o, strum_dn, strum_up]` (sigmoids during training; binary at deploy).
- **Cadence:** runs once per fretboard 240 Hz tick, in the same TC0 callback (`fret_scan_all → model_infer → cmd_apply`). Drops `cmd_receive_update` once the model owns the wire.

### Model

For v1, use **MPLAB ML / SensiML** since their toolchain targets exactly this MCU class:

- Feature extractor: per-channel windowed stats (MAV, std, slope, peaks, simple FIR responses) over the 250 ms window — let SensiML pick the feature set.
- Classifier: gradient-boosted trees or tiny dense NN per output bit (or a single multi-label head if SensiML supports it).

If MPLAB ML's auto-pipeline doesn't get good strum timing, fall back to a tiny **causal 1D-CNN** in TFLM:
- 2 conv layers, ~8 channels, kernel 5–7, dilation `[1, 4]` for ~30-sample receptive field per layer, total RF ≈ window length.
- Hand-quantize to int8.
- Inference budget ~100 k cycles per tick (24 MHz × 4.17 ms ÷ 1) — comfortable for a model with ~1k MACs.

### Window choice — 250 ms

Strum delay = 220 ms = 53 samples. Window of 60 samples (250 ms) gives ~30 ms margin on both ends and lets the model see the strum-relevant photo dip *and* the immediate vicinity for chord shape.

## Why this shape works (sanity-check vs. Greg's concerns)

- **Spatial mismatch dissolved.** No CV-row → photo-row alignment needed. The 250 ms window contains whatever phototransistor signal preceded the current strum, regardless of where on the screen it sits.
- **Strum timing learned.** Strum bits are part of the output. With weighted BCE on the strum bits (they're rare — see "risks" below), the model learns the +220 ms relationship between upstream photo dip and strum-bit assertion.
- **Edge AI is end-to-end standalone.** Once deployed, fretboard runs the model on its own ADC stream; marvin can be off, and gameplay still works. Marvin's role becomes "training data source + reference detector for diagnostics".

## Code changes required

### 1. New label source in the SensiML exporter

Modify [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) to add an `--labels=actuator` mode (default keeps current `--labels=detector` for back-compat):

- Track the most recent `Actuator` record alongside the existing `last_detector`.
- Forward-fill `intended_mask` (7 bits — frets at 0–4, strum-down at 5, strum-up at 6) onto each FretboardRaw row.
- New CSV schema:
  \```
  timestamp, ph_green..ph_orange,
  fret_green..fret_orange, strum_down, strum_up
  \```
- Strum bits are sparse — emit a stat in `ExportStats` ("n_strum_events") so we can sanity-check label density.

The exporter already iterates over decoded records; this is additive and doesn't change FretboardRaw timing logic. New record class `Actuator` may need adding to [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py) (decoder for `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` v3 schema — confirm if not present).

### 2. (Optional, defer) Strike-line CV detector

If Phase-2 validation shows distillation hits a ceiling because marvin's own commands carry too much noise (CDC jitter, chord-window quantisation), add a `cv_strike_v1` detector that samples the strike row directly, and use *its* output as labels instead of `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`. This gives a noiseless 60 Hz oracle, but loses the strum-timing signal, so we'd then re-add a rule-based +0 ms strum-on-strike-cross. Flag for later, don't build now.

### 3. Fretboard runtime integration (later phase)

Add a new module to [firmware/fretboard/](firmware/fretboard/) — `model_infer.c/h` — called from the TC0 callback after `fret_scan_all`. Maintains a 60-sample ring buffer of `fret_scan_result()` outputs across all 5 channels, runs inference, drives the 7 GPIOs directly, and bypasses `cmd_receive_update`.

Operating-mode toggle on fretboard so we can A/B between "marvin-driven" and "model-driven" without reflashing — fretboard SPEC already documents the standalone-fallback mode pattern; this is a third mode.

## Phased rollout

| Phase | Goal | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Data pipeline** | Distillation labels available end-to-end | `--labels=actuator` exporter merged; one captured-gameplay CSV inspected and shows plausible fret + strum timing |
| **2. Host-side baseline model** | Train on PC; validate offline | MPLAB ML / PyTorch model achieves ≥95% per-bit accuracy on held-out song; strum-event timing error p95 ≤ 20 ms (one ADC sample) |
| **3. On-device port** | Same model running on PIC32 | Inference latency < 1 ms (well inside the 4.17 ms tick); on-device output matches host inference bit-for-bit on a recorded ADC trace |
| **4. Side-by-side dry-run** | AI predicts but doesn't drive | New perf-log record for model output; recorded alongside marvin's commands; agreement metrics tracked over a real session |
| **5. Cut-over** | AI drives the controller | Fretboard mode-switch flips wire ownership from `cmd_receive` to `model_infer`; gameplay scoring measured against marvin-driven baseline |

## Risks / things to watch

- **Strum class imbalance.** Strum-up/down bits are 1 for ≤2 ticks per chord, so ~95%+ of samples have strum=0. Need weighted BCE / focal loss / oversampling, or the model will degenerate to "always 0". Verify in Phase 2.
- **Window-too-short failure mode.** If 250 ms doesn't span the photo→strum delay across difficulty levels (Expert scrolls faster, may move the photo dip closer to the strum), strum-bit accuracy will collapse. Sweep window in Phase 2 (125 / 250 / 400 ms).
- **Per-bit independence.** Treating bits as independent sigmoids ignores chord structure; if accuracy is poor, switch to a 32-class softmax over common chord shapes (most chords use few of the 2⁷ combinations).
- **Multi-difficulty training.** Train on Easy + Medium + Expert recordings so scroll-speed variation is in the distribution.
- **Inheriting marvin bugs.** Distillation can't beat the teacher. If marvin mistimes strums, AI mistimes strums. We accept this for v1; phase 6+ can layer human-play recordings on top.

## Open / deferred design questions

- **Hold vs. edge channel per fret.** The 5-channel ADC at 240 Hz may alias on fast notes. Two ways to add information: (a) two photoxistors per fret at different y rows (HW edge detection, "note approaching" + "note here"), or (b) one extra color-filtered photoxistor per fret to mimic CV's color-edge channel. Either doubles ADC scan time. Defer until Phase 2 reveals whether the model is starving for input.
- **AR feedback.** Letting the model see its own recent output as input would help with held-note coherence but adds a feedback loop. Defer.
- **Look-ahead vs. now-cast.** Currently predicting the command at time `T`; could predict `T + K_ms` to give downstream actuators time. Not relevant while output is GPIO (latency ≈ 0); revisit when mechanical actuators land.

## Verification

End-to-end checks per phase:

- **Phase 1** — run `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv`, inspect: row count ≈ 240 × duration, strum bits sparse (~few % set), fret bits dense and matching gameplay difficulty.
- **Phase 2** — train script reports per-bit accuracy and strum timing distribution on the held-out split. Plot predicted vs. true command stream over a 30 s window.
- **Phase 3** — write a unit test that feeds a recorded ADC trace through host inference and on-device inference, asserts identical outputs (or ≤1 LSB after quant).
- **Phase 4** — extend perf-log with `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` (mirrors `Actuator` shape); marvin-perf gains a side-by-side viewer page; agreement metric (Hamming distance per tick) plotted live.
- **Phase 5** — actual game scoring on a fixed song setlist; compare marvin-driven baseline vs. model-driven over 5+ runs each.

# Plan — Author edge-AI design doc

## Context

We've explored the design space for the edge AI subsystem and locked the following:

- **Output shape:** full 1-byte fretboard command (5 fret bits + strum-down + strum-up).
- **Supervision:** distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` from marvin self-play recordings.
- **Deployment target:** fretboard MCU (PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz).
- **Inference inputs:** 5 ADC channels for v1; per-fret expansion deferred.

The key insight is that distilling against marvin's emitted commands (not CV intermediate state) **dissolves the spatial-mismatch problem**: the label is the byte marvin chose with its +220 ms strum delay already baked in, so the model just needs a wide enough causal window to learn whatever delay maps photo dip → strum.

This plan writes that design up as a reviewable doc — not implementation work, just the doc.

## What to build

A single new file: **[firmware/fretboard/docs/edge_ai_spec.md](firmware/fretboard/docs/edge_ai_spec.md)**.

Framed as a *design proposal with open questions surfaced* — readers should be able to push back on specific points.

### Sections

1. **Purpose & scope** — what subsystem this is, what it replaces, what it doesn't.
2. **Why now** — pull-through from Greg's two concerns:
   - Spatial mismatch (CV @ y=311 vs. photoxistor row).
   - Strum timing missing from edge AI's job.
3. **Decisions locked** — the four bullets above, each with a one-line "why".
4. **Architecture**
   - Data flow at training time: marvin records ADC + ACTUATOR → marvin-perf exporter → CSV.
   - Data flow at inference time: fretboard ADC ring → model → 7 GPIOs.
   - Inference cadence (240 Hz, in TC0 callback).
5. **Training pipeline** — concrete code changes:
   - Modify [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) — add `--labels=actuator` mode that forward-fills `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` over FretboardRaw rows.
   - New CSV schema (5 ADC + 7 label cols).
   - Confirm `Actuator` decoder exists in [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py).
6. **Model**
   - Recommendation: 5×60 (250 ms) input, 7-bit output, MPLAB ML / SensiML auto-pipeline first; tiny causal 1D-CNN as fallback.
   - Why 250 ms (covers the +220 ms strum delay with margin).
   - Quant target: int8.
7. **Fretboard runtime integration**
   - New `model_infer.c/h`, ring buffer, replaces `cmd_receive` byte-application.
   - Mode toggle to A/B between marvin-driven and model-driven.
8. **Why this is the right shape** — sanity-check vs. spatial mismatch + strum-timing concerns.
9. **Phased rollout** — five phases (data pipeline → host baseline → on-device port → side-by-side dry run → cut-over) with a "done when" line each.
10. **Risks**
    - Strum class imbalance (strum bits ~5% of samples).
    - Window-too-short across difficulty levels.
    - Per-bit independence vs. chord structure.
    - Multi-difficulty training distribution.
    - Inheriting marvin's bugs.
11. **Open questions** (explicit reviewer-poke list)
    - Q1: Hold vs. edge channel per fret — add HW now, or wait until model is starved?
    - Q2: AR feedback — let model see its own past output?
    - Q3: Look-ahead vs. now-cast — predict at `T + K_ms`?
    - Q4: Strike-line CV detector as alternative label source if distillation hits a noise ceiling?
    - Q5: Phototransistor placement / count — currently 5 above strike, what's optimal?
12. **Alternatives considered (briefly)** — shapes A/B/D from the design exploration (frame classifier with co-located CV, sequence-to-strike-line oracle, two-head event detector). One paragraph each on why C beat them given the locked decisions.
13. **Verification per phase** — how each rollout phase is checked end-to-end.

### Doc style

- Markdown, matches the tone of [firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) and [firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) — sectioned, with file:line citations to existing code.
- Keep code-citation links relative to repo root using markdown link syntax.
- Open questions section should be the first thing a reviewer scans for.

### Cross-references to update (lightweight)

- Add a one-line link from [firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) under the "Tools" or a new "Future work" section pointing at the new doc.
- Add a session-log entry to [firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md](firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md) noting the spec was authored, what's open, and that no code has changed.

## Verification

The doc is good if:

- A reviewer who only knows the system at SPEC.md level can read this end-to-end and understand what we'd build, why this shape, and what we're unsure about.
- The five rollout phases each have an unambiguous "done when".
- The open-questions section invites pushback rather than asking for sign-off.

No code changes in this plan — purely documentation.

# Edge AI — Design Proposal

> **Status:** design proposal, not implemented. Reviewers should push back on the [Open questions](#open-questions) before any code lands.

## 1. Purpose & scope

The edge AI replaces marvin in the runtime gameplay loop with a small ML model running on the fretboard MCU itself. At inference time, fretboard's own 5-channel phototransistor ADC stream is the only input; the model emits the same 1-byte fret + strum bitmask that marvin's timing pipeline produces today, applied directly to the controller GPIOs.

**In scope:**

- A model architecture, training pipeline, and on-device runtime that, once trained, lets the fretboard run gameplay end-to-end without marvin.
- Training-data plumbing on marvin and in [tools/marvin-perf/](../../../tools/marvin-perf/).

**Out of scope:**

- Replacing marvin as the *reference* detector. Marvin remains the source of truth for training and diagnostics.
- Game-state / menu navigation. The edge AI plays gameplay only; whole-session control still belongs to marvin (system [SPEC.md §4.8 of marvin spec](../../marvin/docs/spec.md)).
- The fretboard-takeover fallback ([fretboard/docs/journal.md](journal.md), 2026-06-02 entry). That mode runs `fret_button.c` standalone; the edge AI is a third operating mode alongside it.

## 2. Why now

Two concrete pressures came out of the recent training-data work:

### 2.1 Spatial mismatch

The current SensiML CSV exporter ([tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py)) labels each fretboard ADC sample with `cv_marvin_v1`'s `pressed_mask`, broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`. But the two sensors look at different points on the screen:

- `cv_marvin_v1` samples at `y = 311` ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](../../marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)), above the strike line.
- The five phototransistors physically sit "above the TV strike line" ([SPEC.md §Sensor Inputs](../SPEC.md)), at a different (unverified) row than `y = 311`.

Same falling note, different sensors, different times. Aligning them on `frame_epoch` bakes in a fixed offset that is only correct at one scroll speed. Fixing this in hardware (move the photoxistors, or move the CV row) is finicky and locks the system to a single mechanical layout.

### 2.2 Strum timing missing from the AI's job

Today's training pipeline emits per-fret pressed labels only. The chord window + +220 ms strum scheduler ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c:21,198,199](../../marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) is real, non-trivial work that the AI is not being asked to learn. Whatever the AI replaces, the timing pipeline still has to live somewhere.

## 3. Decisions locked

| Decision | Why (one line) |
|---|---|
| **Output:** the full 1-byte fretboard command — 5 fret bits + strum-down (bit 5) + strum-up (bit 6). | Pulls strum timing into the AI; matches the existing wire protocol ([cmd_receive.c](../cmd_receive.c)). |
| **Supervision:** distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` from marvin self-play. | Sidesteps spatial mismatch — labels are marvin's chosen byte, not a CV intermediate. |
| **Deployment target:** fretboard PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz. | Removes marvin from the gameplay loop; truly "edge". |
| **Inputs at inference (v1):** the existing 5 ADC channels only. | Cheapest start; per-fret HW expansion deferred to [Q1](#q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret). |
| **Training corpus:** marvin self-play recordings only. | Simplest closure; AI inherits marvin's behavior (good and bad — see [§10 risks](#10-risks)). |

The key insight that makes this work: **distilling against marvin's commands dissolves the spatial-mismatch problem.** The label is the byte marvin chose with the +220 ms strum delay already baked in. The model just needs a wide enough causal window of ADC to learn whatever delay maps photo dip → strum, regardless of where the photoxistors physically sit. Mechanical alignment becomes a non-requirement.

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Training-time data flow

\```
Wii ──► marvin (cv_marvin_v1 + timing_pipeline)
          │   │
          │   ├── PERF_REC_ACTUATOR (intended_mask, strum_dir)   ──┐
          │   └── (commands over USB CDC to fretboard)              │
          │                                                          ▼
          │                                                  marvin-perf
          │                                                  (offline)
          │   ▲                                                      │
          │   │ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (5×ADC @ 240 Hz)              │
          │   │                                                      │
          │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
          │                                                          │
          │                                                          ▼
          │                                                   SensiML CSV
          │                                            (per-row: 5 ADC + 7 labels)
\```

Both record streams already flow through perf-log keyed by `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`. The exporter joins them offline.

### 4.2 Inference-time data flow

\```
fretboard TC0 callback @ 240 Hz:
    fret_scan_all()             ──► s_adc_ring[60][5]    (250 ms history)
                                       │
                                       ▼
                                 model_infer(ring) ──► uint8_t cmd_byte
                                       │
                                       ▼
                                 button_apply(cmd_byte)  (open-drain GPIOs)
\```

`cmd_receive_update()` is bypassed when fretboard is in model-driven mode; the model owns the wire instead of marvin.

### 4.3 Inference cadence

One inference per 240 Hz tick (every 4.17 ms), called inline from the existing TC0 callback after `fret_scan_all` and before `button_apply`. Budget per inference at 24 MHz with no FPU is ≈100 k cycles — comfortable for a model with ≲1 k MACs at int8.

## 5. Training pipeline

### 5.1 New label source in the SensiML exporter

Modify [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) to add an `--labels=actuator` mode (the current `pressed_mask` path stays as `--labels=detector` for back-compat):

- Track the most recent `Actuator` record alongside `last_detector` (decoder already exists at [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py:300](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py)).
- Forward-fill `Actuator.intended_mask` (7 bits — frets at 0..4, strum-down at 5, strum-up at 6) onto each `FretboardRaw` row.
- Emit a per-export stat `n_strum_events` so we can verify strum-bit density on a captured corpus.

### 5.2 New CSV schema

\```
timestamp,
ph_green, ph_red, ph_yellow, ph_blue, ph_orange,
fret_green, fret_red, fret_yellow, fret_blue, fret_orange,
strum_down, strum_up
\```

Same row cadence as today (one row per `FretboardRaw` ≈ 240 Hz).

### 5.3 Capture protocol

A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures across difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Expert) and song variety. Each capture must have all of `SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW` enabled in the `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`.

## 6. Model

### 6.1 Recommended baseline

- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × 60 samples (250 ms causal window) @ 240 Hz, int16 → int8 after normalisation.
- **Output:** 7 sigmoids during training (independent BCE per bit); thresholded to binary at deploy.
- **Architecture:** MPLAB ML / SensiML auto-pipeline first — windowed feature extractor (MAV, std, slope, peak, simple FIR taps) feeding a gradient-boosted ensemble or tiny dense head. SensiML targets exactly this MCU class.
- **Fallback if auto-pipeline misses strum timing:** tiny causal 1D-CNN, two conv layers ~8 channels, kernel 5–7, dilation `[1, 4]`. Quantise to int8.

### 6.2 Why 250 ms

`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` ([timing_pipeline.c:21](../../marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)). 60 samples × 4.17 ms = 250 ms gives ≈30 ms margin around the photo-dip-to-strum-bit relationship. Window length is the most important hyperparameter to sweep in [phase 2](#phase-2--host-side-baseline) — see [Q3](#q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast).

### 6.3 Quantisation

int8 weights, int16 activations during the conv layers, int8 at the output. PIC32CM has no FPU; floating-point inference is a non-starter.

## 7. Fretboard runtime integration

### 7.1 New module

Add `model_infer.c` / `model_infer.h` to [firmware/fretboard/](..) alongside the existing modules:

- Owns the 60-sample × 5-channel ring buffer.
- `model_infer_push(uint16_t adc[5])` called from the TC0 callback after `fret_scan_all`.
- `model_infer_run()` returns a `uint8_t` command byte.

### 7.2 TC0 callback shape

\```
TC0 callback (240 Hz)
    fret_scan_all()
    data_stream_send()                   // diagnostic, optional in model mode
    if (mode == MODEL_DRIVEN) {
        model_infer_push(scan_results)
        cmd = model_infer_run()
        button_apply(cmd)
    } else {
        cmd_receive_update()             // marvin-driven (today's path)
    }
\```

### 7.3 Operating-mode toggle

A new fretboard operating mode `MODEL_DRIVEN` joins the existing `MARVIN_DRIVEN` (today's default) and the dormant `STANDALONE` (the orphaned `fret_button.c` fallback). Switch lives in `main.c`'s init or a build-time `#define` for v1; runtime toggle deferred to phase 4.

## 8. Why this shape (sanity-check)

- **Spatial mismatch dissolved.** No CV-row → photo-row alignment needed at training time. The 250 ms window captures whatever upstream signal preceded the strum, regardless of physical sensor placement.
- **Strum timing learned.** Strum bits are part of the output. Weighted BCE on the strum bits (which are sparse — see [§10](#10-risks)) lets the model learn the +220 ms photo-to-strum delay implicitly.
- **Edge AI is end-to-end standalone.** Once deployed, fretboard runs the model on its own ADC stream; marvin can be off and gameplay still works. Marvin's role becomes "training-data source + reference detector for diagnostics + game-state controller".

## 9. Phased rollout

| Phase | Goal | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Data pipeline** | Distillation labels available end-to-end | `--labels=actuator` exporter merged; one captured-gameplay CSV inspected and shows plausible fret + strum timing |
| **2. Host-side baseline** | Train on PC; validate offline | MPLAB ML / PyTorch model achieves ≥95% per-bit accuracy on held-out song; strum-event timing error p95 ≤ 20 ms (one ADC sample) |
| **3. On-device port** | Same model running on PIC32 | Inference latency < 1 ms (well inside the 4.17 ms tick); on-device output matches host inference bit-for-bit on a recorded ADC trace (within int8 quant tolerance) |
| **4. Side-by-side dry-run** | AI predicts but doesn't drive | New perf-log record `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` mirrors `Actuator` shape; recorded alongside marvin's commands; per-tick agreement tracked over a real session |
| **5. Cut-over** | AI drives the controller | Fretboard mode-switch flips wire ownership from `cmd_receive` to `model_infer`; gameplay scoring measured against marvin-driven baseline |

<a id="phase-2--host-side-baseline"></a>

## 10. Risks

- **Strum class imbalance.** Strum-up/down bits are 1 for ≤2 ticks per chord, so the great majority of samples have strum=0. Weighted BCE / focal loss / oversampling required — verify in phase 2 that the model isn't degenerating to "always 0".
- **Window-too-short failure mode.** If 250 ms doesn't span the photo-dip-to-strum-bit delay across difficulty levels (Expert scrolls faster — photo dip is closer to the strum), strum-bit accuracy collapses. Sweep window in phase 2 (125 / 250 / 400 ms).
- **Per-bit independence vs. chord structure.** Treating bits as independent sigmoids ignores that real chords occupy a tiny subset of the 2⁷ space. If accuracy is poor, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes.
- **Multi-difficulty distribution.** Train on Easy + Medium + Expert recordings; otherwise scroll-speed variation is out of distribution.
- **Inheriting marvin's bugs.** Distillation can't beat the teacher. Mistimed strums in marvin become mistimed strums in the AI. Acceptable for v1; future work could layer human-play recordings on top (see [Q4](#q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source)).
- **CDC + RTOS jitter in labels.** `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` timestamps the moment marvin emits the command, not the moment fretboard physically asserts the GPIO. There's some milliseconds of jitter from USB host scheduling and fretboard RX polling baked into the labels. Probably fine — fretboard saw that same jitter at runtime — but worth measuring.

## 11. Open questions

> Reviewers: this is the section to push back on. Each question is a real fork.

<a id="q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret"></a>
### Q1: Hold vs. edge channel per fret — add HW now, or wait?

The current 5-channel ADC at 240 Hz may alias on fast transients. Two ways to add information:

- **(a)** Two photoxistors per fret at *different* screen rows — gives the model an intrinsic "note approaching" + "note here" pair, doubling temporal resolution at hardware cost.
- **(b)** One extra photoxistor per fret with a colour filter, mimicking `cv_marvin_v1`'s colour-edge channel — separates "any brightness here" from "specifically a green note here".

Either doubles the ADC scan time. Bias is to start with the existing 5 channels and only add HW if phase 2 shows the model is starved for input.

<a id="q2-ar-feedback"></a>
### Q2: AR feedback — let the model see its own past output?

Most fret-bit predictions at time `T` are highly correlated with the prediction at `T-1` (held notes). An AR model could be much smaller / more accurate. Cost: a feedback loop at runtime (bugs amplify), and harder training (teacher forcing vs. scheduled sampling). Defer until non-AR baseline is known.

<a id="q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast"></a>
### Q3: Look-ahead vs. now-cast — predict at T+K?

Currently formulated as "predict the command at *now*". Could instead predict at `T + K_ms` to cover model+actuator latency. Irrelevant while actuators are GPIOs (latency ≈ 0); revisit when mechanical actuators land ([SPEC.md §5](../../../SPEC.md), `hardware/actuators/`).

<a id="q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source"></a>
### Q4: Strike-line CV detector as alternative label source?

If phase 2 reveals that distillation hits a noise ceiling (CDC jitter + chord-window quantisation), an alternative is to add a `cv_strike_v1` detector that samples the *strike row* directly at 60 Hz. Cleaner labels for fret state, but loses strum-event timing — would need to re-add a rule-based "strum when strike row goes active". Flag for now, don't build.

<a id="q5-photoxistor-placement"></a>
### Q5: Phototransistor placement / count — what's optimal?

Today's PCB ([hardware/Sensor-LCD5/](../../../hardware/Sensor-LCD5/)) has 5 sensors above the strike line. Optimum-for-this-AI is unknown:

- *Higher* on the screen → longer lookahead but more time for the note appearance to change.
- *At the strike line* → simplest label (the photo dip *is* the answer) but no anticipation, breaking strum scheduling.
- *Two rows* → see [Q1](#q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret).

Open until phase 2 data tells us which placement makes the model's job easiest.

## 12. Alternatives considered

Three other shapes were on the table before the C / distillation choice landed:

- **Shape A — frame classifier with co-located CV.** Model predicts `pressed_mask` from a single ADC sample; labels come from a *new* CV detector at the photoxistor row. Pros: small model, easy to label. Rejected because it still leaves the strum decision outside the AI, and forces mechanical alignment between CV and photoxistors — exactly the problem we're trying to dissolve.
- **Shape B — sequence-to-strike-line oracle.** Model takes a causal ADC window, outputs what's at the strike row right now. Labels come from a new strike-row CV detector. Pros: clean physical meaning ("predict the moment of truth"). Rejected because, like A, it doesn't include strum timing — a downstream rule still has to schedule strums. We'd be solving the easier half of the problem twice.
- **Shape D — two-head (continuous fret + sparse strum events).** One head for held-note state, one head for `[time-to-strum, mask, dir]` events. Closer to the underlying physics. Rejected as v1 because it's significantly more complex to architect, train, and validate. **Worth revisiting if the per-bit-independence loss in shape C produces poor strum timing in phase 2** — D's sparse-event head is a natural cure.

## 13. Verification per phase

- **Phase 1** — `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv`; manually inspect: row count ≈ 240 × duration_s, strum bits sparse (a few %), fret bits dense and matching gameplay difficulty.
- **Phase 2** — training script reports per-bit accuracy and strum-event timing distribution on the held-out split. Plot predicted vs. true command stream over a 30 s window; visually verify chord+strum alignment.
- **Phase 3** — unit test feeds a recorded ADC trace through host inference and on-device inference, asserts identical outputs (or ≤1 LSB diff after quant).
- **Phase 4** — extend perf-log with `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` (mirrors `Actuator` shape); marvin-perf gains a side-by-side viewer; per-tick Hamming distance between model output and marvin output is logged live.
- **Phase 5** — actual game scoring on a fixed song setlist (Easy + Medium + Expert), 5+ runs each: marvin-driven baseline vs. model-driven. Pass if model-driven scores within X% of baseline (X to be set by reviewer).
